item.title: Adyen
item.description: Adyen offers a single payments system that covers the entire flow, from the checkout page to the bank. It works as the payment processor and acquirer, which means it connects directly to card networks instead of relying on separate providers, and supports a wide range of payment methods including local options like iDEAL and Alipay. Large retailers, marketplaces, and subscription companies use it to accept payments in many countries with a unified view of the data.

item.title: Altium Designer
item.description:
Altium Designer is a professional environment for designing electronics. Engineers draw circuit schematics, lay out the physical board with components and traces, check the design against rules for manufacturing and signal integrity, and generate the files that fabricators need. It supports complex, high-speed, and multi-layer boards used in consumer devices, medical equipment, aerospace, and automotive electronics.

Collaboration and cloud tools extend the desktop product. Altium 365 provides a platform for sharing designs, managing components, and reviewing changes with teammates and manufacturers, and integrations with mechanical CAD allow electrical and mechanical engineers to work together. Component libraries and supply chain data help pick parts that are available. Newer features bring in AI-assisted capabilities, such as automating parts of layout or helping with design checks.

item.title: Apple Vision Pro
item.description:
Vision Pro puts a computer in front of your eyes. High-resolution displays and cameras show the real world with digital windows and objects placed in it, and you interact by looking at things and pinching your fingers, with no controllers needed. It runs visionOS and supports iPad and Apple apps, along with apps made for spatial computing, such as immersive video, 3D design, and games.

Typical uses include watching movies on a giant virtual screen, working with multiple floating windows, viewing and recording spatial photos and videos, and previewing 3D models. Mac Virtual Display mirrors a Mac into the headset, and enterprise users explore training, design review, and remote collaboration. Apple Intelligence features are being added to visionOS, including writing tools and a smarter Siri, and the device’s sensors power features like hand tracking and scene understanding.

item.title: Archistar
item.description:
Archistar addresses the slow, rule-heavy process of getting buildings approved. Its platform reads planning regulations and site data to show what can be built on a lot, such as height, setbacks, and density. Developers and architects can test ideas and see the potential of a site before they invest.

For design checking, the tool compares a proposed building against local codes and flags issues, which reduces the back and forth with planning authorities. Councils use it to review applications faster and with more consistency. Generative design features create massing options that fit the rules, and reports summarize feasibility.

item.title: AudioEye
item.description:
AudioEye is a web accessibility service. Its scanner tests pages against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines, finding problems such as missing alt text, poor contrast, unlabeled form fields, and keyboard traps. A script added to the site can then apply fixes automatically for many of these issues, which is quicker than editing every page by hand.

Automation covers only part of the job, so AudioEye also offers expert audits, user testing with people who have disabilities, and managed services. It provides monitoring, reports, and accessibility statements, and integrates with common platforms like Shopify and WordPress. Companies use it to show a good faith effort toward compliance.

item.title: Auth0
item.description: Auth0 saves developers from building login systems themselves, which is a task where mistakes are costly. You add its SDK to an app, and it handles sign-up, login, password reset, social logins like Google or Apple, and passwordless options such as one-time codes and passkeys. It can connect to company identity providers for single sign-on, apply multi-factor and adaptive authentication, and manage roles and permissions. A hosted login page can be customized to match your brand.

item.title: AVEVA
item.description:
AVEVA serves heavy industry with software for designing and running plants. Engineering tools support the design of facilities such as refineries and power stations in 3D, process simulation helps engineers model how plants will behave, and operations software monitors and controls equipment in real time. The PI System, which it acquired through OSIsoft, collects and stores time-series data from industrial sensors across thousands of sites.

AI and analytics sit on top of this data. Predictive analytics monitor equipment for early signs of failure, and optimization tools help reduce energy use and improve throughput. Industrial AI assistants help operators and engineers search documents and data, and digital twin capabilities connect engineering models with live operations. The company’s AVEVA Connect cloud platform brings these tools together.

item.title: Azure AI Vision
item.description:
Azure AI Vision gives developers pretrained image analysis. The Image Analysis service can describe an image in a sentence, tag objects and scenes, detect people and objects with locations, and extract printed and handwritten text through OCR. Additional capabilities include background removal, smart cropping, and searching images by meaning, using models that understand both text and images.

Video and spatial analysis features can analyze camera feeds to count people and measure how they move through physical spaces, useful in retail and building management. Face-related features exist but are limited by a responsible AI approval process, since facial recognition has privacy and fairness concerns. Customers can also train custom models for their own image categories, and containers allow running some features on the edge.

item.title: Ben's Bites
item.description:
Ben’s Bites began as a daily email in which Ben Tossell shared what he found interesting in AI. It became popular because he wrote like a person rather than a press release, picking tools worth trying and giving short reactions. Readers range from founders and developers to curious non-technical people who want to keep up.

Over time, it expanded beyond a single email. A community of subscribers shares tips and projects, and there are resources such as prompt collections and a list of tools. Some content is for paying members, while the main newsletter remains free. Sponsorships support the free edition and are labeled.

item.title: Better Stack
item.description:
Better Stack started with uptime monitoring, checking websites and APIs and alerting the team when something fails. It has since added more of the operations toolkit. Telemetry covers logs and metrics, with fast search over large volumes, and incident management handles on-call schedules and escalation, with calls, texts, and chat alerts.

Public and private status pages let companies tell customers what is going on during an outage. The pieces work together: a failed check can open an incident, notify the person on call, and update the status page. The pitch is lower cost and less setup than assembling Datadog, PagerDuty, and Statuspage.

item.title: Blackbaud
item.description:
Blackbaud is one of the largest vendors serving the social good sector. Its Raiser’s Edge NXT is a widely used fundraising and donor management system that tracks supporters, gifts, campaigns, and relationships, with tools for prospect research and online giving. Other products handle accounting, grants management, school administration, volunteer management, and corporate giving programs.

AI has been added across the line. Blackbaud Intelligence helps predict donors who are likely to give more, recommends who to contact, and drafts fundraising messages, and assistants help staff query data and build reports. Integrations connect with email, payment, and analytics tools. As a major data holder, Blackbaud has had to handle security responsibilities, including responding to a ransomware incident that affected customers.

item.title: Bruno
item.description:
Bruno is part of the group of tools for sending API requests, alongside Postman and Insomnia. Its approach is different: collections are saved in a plain text markup language as files in a folder, not in a vendor’s cloud. Teams commit them to git, review changes in pull requests, and keep API tests next to the code they test.

You can build requests with variables, scripts, and assertions, run collections for testing, and use it from a command line interface in CI pipelines. It supports REST, GraphQL, and other protocols. Because it works offline and does not require an account, it appeals to developers who dislike mandatory sign-ins and cloud syncing after changes in other tools.

item.title: Bumble
item.description:
Bumble set itself apart by changing who starts the conversation. When a man and a woman match, the woman has to send the first message within a time limit, which the company says reduces unwanted messages and gives women more control. In same-sex matches, either person can begin. The app uses the swipe format, and offers filters for interests, intentions, and distance.

Beyond dating, Bumble has modes to meet friends and to network professionally, though these have been less central to its success. Safety features include photo verification, a feature that detects and blurs unwanted nude images, and tools for reporting and blocking. AI is used to detect fake profiles, spam, and scams, and to flag harassing messages, which are persistent problems for dating apps.

item.title: CARTO
item.description:
CARTO focuses on location data at scale. Instead of copying data to a separate tool, it works where the data already lives, using the warehouse’s compute. Analysts can run spatial operations such as joins, clustering, and routing, and build interactive maps that stay connected to live data.

The platform has three common uses. Analysts build maps and dashboards to explore patterns, data teams construct workflows with a visual editor for spatial processing, and developers embed maps and analytics into applications through APIs. Datasets for demographics, points of interest, and mobility are available to enrich internal data. AI agents let users ask spatial questions in natural language.

item.title: CertiK
item.description:
CertiK works on security for blockchain projects. Its core service is the audit, in which engineers and automated tools review a project’s smart contract code to find bugs, logic mistakes, and vulnerabilities before funds are at risk. Audit reports are often published, and projects display them to build trust with users.

Beyond audits, CertiK offers monitoring and scoring. Its Skynet platform tracks security signals and rates projects, and it provides alerts, wallet and transaction analysis, and tools for investigating hacks. Bug bounty programs and penetration testing add other layers, and it also offers formal verification for high-assurance contracts.

item.title: Chainalysis
item.description:
Chainalysis makes sense of public blockchains. Cryptocurrency transactions are visible but pseudonymous, which makes it hard to know who is behind an address. Chainalysis clusters addresses, identifies services such as exchanges and mixers, and links activity to known entities using a large body of data and heuristics. Investigators can follow funds through a chain of transfers, and compliance teams can check whether a transaction touches risky or sanctioned counterparties.

Its products serve distinct users. Reactor is an investigation tool used by law enforcement and security teams, KYT (Know Your Transaction) monitors transactions for exchanges and financial institutions, and other tools support risk scoring, sanctions screening, and reporting. The company publishes research on crypto crime trends, which is widely cited. Machine learning helps detect patterns of illicit behavior and attribute clusters of activity.

item.title: CoachHub
item.description:
CoachHub is a digital coaching platform sold to employers. Employees are matched with certified coaches for one-on-one sessions on topics such as leadership, communication, and career growth. Sessions take place by video, and the company offers coaches across many countries and languages.

Between sessions, an AI coach named AIMY supports employees. It is available for quick conversations, helps rehearse difficult discussions, and supports goal setting, extending coaching beyond what a limited number of human sessions can cover. The platform reports on usage and progress to the sponsoring company.

item.title: Cvent
item.description:
Cvent is one of the most widely used enterprise event management suites. Planners create event websites and registration forms, collect payments, manage agendas and speakers, and communicate with attendees. A venue sourcing marketplace helps find hotels and meeting spaces and request proposals, which is a central part of corporate meeting planning, and tools handle housing blocks and travel for attendees.

On site and after the event, it provides engagement and measurement. Mobile apps, check-in, and badge printing run the day, while surveys and analytics measure attendance and satisfaction. AI features help generate event content, match attendees for networking, and assist with planning tasks, and integrations connect with CRMs and marketing automation to link events to pipeline. It supports in-person, virtual, and hybrid formats.

item.title: Digital Diagnostics
item.description:
Digital Diagnostics offers autonomous AI for eye screening. A clinic staff member takes photos of a patient’s retina with a compatible camera, the software analyzes the images, and within minutes the clinic gets a result: either the screening is negative, or the patient should see an eye specialist. No ophthalmologist needs to read the images.

That matters because many people with diabetes skip yearly eye exams, and early detection of retinopathy prevents vision loss. Putting screening in a primary care office makes it easier to catch disease. The company also develops AI for other conditions and works with health systems on implementation and billing.

item.title: Dotmatics
item.description:
Dotmatics sells a connected software platform for laboratories. Scientists record experiments in electronic notebooks, manage samples and compounds, analyze results, and search data across projects. The aim is to link research data that would otherwise be spread across spreadsheets and separate instruments, so teams can find and reuse it.

The company has assembled a portfolio of well-known science tools. SnapGene supports molecular biology, GraphPad Prism is a standard for statistical analysis and graphs, Geneious handles sequence analysis, and other products cover chemistry, biology, and lab informatics. Machine learning and analytics features help with tasks such as modeling and data search.

item.title: Dynatrace
item.description:
Dynatrace is one of the established names in monitoring large, complex IT environments. A single agent, OneAgent, installs on servers, containers, and cloud services and automatically discovers applications and their dependencies, then collects metrics, traces, logs, and user experience data without much manual setup. A model of how components relate, kept up to date automatically, lets the platform see how a slowdown in one service affects others.

Its distinguishing feature is Davis AI. Instead of only alerting when thresholds are crossed, Davis uses causal analysis to identify the likely root cause of a problem and the business impact, reducing the pile of alerts into a smaller number of actionable issues. Newer generative AI features let users ask questions in natural language, and the platform adds automation that can trigger remediation. Dynatrace also covers security, application vulnerabilities, and monitoring of AI workloads.

item.title: Envision
item.description:
Envision uses AI to help blind and low-vision people with everyday visual tasks. Users point a phone or wearable camera at printed text, a product, or a scene and hear it read or described aloud. It can read documents, scan barcodes, recognize faces of saved contacts, and identify colors and objects.

The glasses offer hands-free use, with a camera worn at head level and spoken output, which suits tasks like reading mail or navigating a new place. An assistant lets users ask follow-up questions about what the camera sees, and a calling feature reaches sighted helpers when AI is not enough.

item.title: Excalidraw
item.description: Excalidraw has a distinct look: lines and shapes appear as if drawn by hand, which lowers the pressure to make diagrams perfect and encourages quick sketching. It runs in the browser without an account. You draw boxes, arrows, and text, drop in shapes from libraries, and share a link so others can edit with you in real time. It’s popular with developers for architecture sketches and with teachers and designers for brainstorming.

item.title: Finastra
item.description:
Finastra supplies the systems that sit behind a bank’s services. Its portfolio includes core banking platforms, commercial and retail lending, payments, trade finance, and treasury and capital markets tools. Banks of different sizes use it, from community institutions to global groups, and often run Finastra systems for decades.

The company has been moving customers toward the cloud and open banking. Its FusionFabric.cloud platform lets banks and third-party developers build apps and connect to Finastra’s services through APIs, and it has been adding AI features for tasks such as credit analysis, document processing, and customer service. Partnerships with large cloud providers support hosting.

item.title: Foxglove
item.description:
Foxglove helps robotics teams understand what their machines did. Robots generate streams from cameras, lidar, GPS, motors, and logs, and debugging requires looking at them together on a timeline. Foxglove’s viewer shows images, point clouds, plots, maps, and 3D scenes in customizable panels that stay synchronized, and it works with ROS and other frameworks.

The platform adds data management. Teams upload recordings to the cloud, search across them by metadata and events, share links to specific moments, and collaborate on issues. The company also created MCAP, an open container format for multimodal robotics data that is now used widely, including as the default recording format in ROS 2.

item.title: Garmin Pilot
item.description:
Garmin Pilot covers the same ground as other flight apps. Pilots plan routes, get weather and notices to air missions, file flight plans, and carry charts and approach procedures on a tablet. In flight, it displays a moving map, traffic, and weather from compatible receivers.

Its advantage is integration with Garmin hardware. The app connects to Garmin avionics and portable devices, so flight plans can be sent to the aircraft’s navigator and data flows both ways. Features such as terrain awareness and flight data logging round out the toolset.

item.title: Grafana
item.description: Grafana is the dashboard tool many engineering teams reach for first. It connects to data sources such as Prometheus, Loki, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, and cloud monitoring services, and lets you build panels and dashboards that visualize time-series data, with alerts that notify teams when something goes wrong. Because it does not store data itself, it can sit on top of whatever you already collect, which is a major reason it is so widely adopted.

item.title: H&R Block
item.description:
H&R Block is one of the largest tax preparation brands in the United States. Customers can file themselves with online software, which asks questions, imports tax documents, and calculates returns, or go to one of thousands of offices where a tax professional prepares the return. A middle option connects people with an expert online who can answer questions or complete the return for them.

AI shows up as an assistant that answers tax questions in plain language, helps find deductions and credits, and explains forms, working within the tax software and drawing on the company’s tax knowledge. Other features include importing prior-year returns, audit support, and refund tracking. The company also provides services such as small business tax and bookkeeping.

item.title: Headway
item.description:
Headway offers book summaries you can read or listen to in minutes. Each summary covers the main ideas of a nonfiction title, such as business, psychology, or self-improvement, so users can sample many books quickly. Audio versions suit commutes and workouts.

The app leans on habit building. Users set daily goals, track streaks, and get reminders, and collections organize summaries by theme and goal. Quizzes and flashcards help retain what was read, and AI features personalize recommendations.

item.title: Icertis
item.description:
Icertis helps big companies manage a very large volume of contracts. Its platform stores contracts in a central repository, supports authoring from templates and clause libraries, routes agreements for approval, and tracks obligations after signing, so deadlines and commitments are not missed. Customers use it for sales, procurement, partner, and employment agreements across many countries.

AI is a core part of the pitch. The Icertis Contract Intelligence platform reads agreements to extract key terms, flags risky or nonstandard language, and compares contracts against playbooks. Generative AI features answer questions about a contract portfolio, summarize agreements, and assist with drafting, and the company has expanded its capabilities through acquisitions. It integrates with enterprise systems such as Salesforce, SAP, and Microsoft.

item.title: Infura
item.description:
Infura gives developers a dependable way to talk to blockchains. Running a node means maintaining servers, storage, and synchronization, so many projects prefer to use an API instead. Infura offers JSON-RPC and WebSocket endpoints for Ethereum, layer 2 networks, and other chains, letting apps read data, send transactions, and subscribe to events through a single key.

The service includes extras. Support for IPFS provides decentralized file storage, and features such as gas estimation and network monitoring help developers. Because Infura is part of Consensys, which also makes MetaMask, it is deeply integrated into much of the Ethereum ecosystem, and a lot of wallets and applications depend on it.

item.title: Insight Timer
item.description:
Insight Timer is known for its sheer size and its free offering. The app hosts a huge collection of guided meditations on topics such as stress, sleep, anxiety, and focus, along with music tracks, talks, and live events with teachers worldwide. A simple timer with bells is at the heart of the app, from which it takes its name, and it supports daily streaks and a community of users.

The free library covers most needs, which sets it apart from subscription-first apps like Calm and Headspace. A paid membership unlocks structured courses, offline downloads, advanced filters, and other features, and teachers can earn money from their content. Search and recommendations help sort through the volume of content, and some AI features support discovery and personalization.

item.title: KAYAK
item.description:
KAYAK doesn’t sell travel itself. Instead, it searches airlines, online travel agencies, and hotel sites at once and shows the options in one place, with filters for price, stops, airlines, and times. When you pick an option, it sends you to the provider to book. This saves time compared with checking many sites individually, and the interface offers flexible date grids and nearby airport searches to find cheaper alternatives.

Several tools help with timing and decisions. Price alerts notify you when a fare changes, and forecasts indicate whether prices are likely to rise or fall, so you can choose between booking now or waiting. KAYAK also offers trip planning, a Trips organizer for itineraries, and filters for things like total cost including bag fees. Conversational AI search lets you describe a trip in plain language and get suggestions.

item.title: KiCad
item.description:
KiCad is the most popular open-source tool for designing printed circuit boards. Engineers draw schematics, assign components, lay out the board with traces and layers, and generate the files that manufacturers need, such as Gerbers and drill files. A 3D viewer shows how the finished board will look, and checks for design rules help catch errors before fabrication. It handles professional designs with many layers and high-speed signals.

The project has strong community and institutional backing. It is developed by volunteers and professionals, with support from organizations like CERN, and has a large library of symbols, footprints, and 3D models. Plugins and scripting in Python extend it, and manufacturers such as PCB fabricators provide direct support. Recent releases have improved the interface, simulation, and collaboration.

item.title: Kinexon
item.description:
Kinexon is a real-time location system. Small sensors worn by athletes or attached to a ball or a piece of equipment communicate with fixed anchors around a venue, and the system calculates positions many times per second. Teams use the data to measure distance, speed, accelerations, and tactical positioning.

In sports, coaches and sports scientists monitor workload to manage fatigue and reduce injury risk, and analysts study movement patterns. The company has been used in leagues for handball, basketball, hockey, football, and others. Broadcasters use the tracking data for graphics.

item.title: Label Studio
item.description:
Label Studio is a flexible annotation platform. Teams use it to label data for machine learning, such as drawing boxes on images, tagging entities in text, transcribing audio, and rating language model outputs. Its configuration system lets users define custom labeling interfaces with simple markup, so one tool can serve a wide range of projects, and it runs locally or on a server.

Model-assisted labeling speeds up work. A machine learning backend can pre-label data for humans to correct, and active learning helps prioritize the most informative examples. The platform supports evaluating language models, with templates for tasks like ranking responses and checking for factual errors, which has become a common use as teams build AI applications. An API and SDK connect it with training pipelines.

item.title: Magnet Forensics
item.description:
Magnet Forensics serves police, government agencies, and corporate investigators. Its flagship product, Magnet AXIOM, gathers data from devices and online accounts and organizes it so examiners can search messages, photos, browsing history, and app data. Timelines and artifacts help reconstruct what happened and produce reports for legal use.

The company has grown through combination. It merged with Grayshift, which makes tools for accessing locked mobile devices, and offers related products for acquiring evidence, triaging devices at a scene, and reviewing cases collaboratively. AI features help classify images, detect relevant content, and speed up the review of large volumes of data.

item.title: MasterControl
item.description:
MasterControl serves regulated manufacturers, such as pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies. Its quality management system handles documents, training, change control, deviations, and corrective actions in a way that satisfies FDA and international rules. Electronic records and signatures provide the audit trail regulators expect.

The platform extends to manufacturing. Electronic batch records and production tools capture how products are made, connecting quality data to the shop floor. AI features help review documents, find trends in quality events, and speed up routine tasks.

item.title: Merlin Bird ID
item.description:
Merlin makes bird identification easy for beginners and experts. You can answer a few questions about where and when you saw a bird, its size, colors, and behavior, and Merlin suggests species. Photo ID uses image recognition to name a bird from a picture, and Sound ID listens to birdsong through your phone’s microphone in real time and shows which species are singing, which many users find astonishing.

The app is built on data from eBird, a huge citizen science project where birdwatchers log sightings, and machine learning trained on millions of photos and recordings. Downloadable regional packs let you identify birds without cell service, which helps in the field. Each species has photos, sounds, maps, and information, and a life list lets you track birds you have seen.

item.title: MetaHuman
item.description:
MetaHuman made high-quality digital humans available to everyone. In MetaHuman Creator, you start from presets and adjust facial features, skin, hair, eyes, teeth, and clothing, and get a fully rigged character with realistic details that works with Unreal Engine. Instead of weeks of sculpting and rigging, a studio or hobbyist can have a believable character in a short time.

Other tools expand what you can create. Mesh to MetaHuman converts a scan or custom model into a MetaHuman, MetaHuman Animator turns an iPhone or head-mounted camera recording of an actor’s performance into detailed facial animation, and characters can be used in games, films, virtual production, and training. Epic has expanded where MetaHumans can be used, including in other 3D tools and engines under its license terms, and Epic’s Fab marketplace sells related assets.

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID
item.description:
Entra ID is the identity system behind most Microsoft cloud accounts. When someone signs in to Microsoft 365, Teams, or Azure, Entra ID checks who they are and what they may access. It provides single sign-on to thousands of third-party apps, manages users and groups, and supports multi-factor authentication, passwordless sign-in with passkeys and authenticator apps, and device registration.

The security features are a key reason companies use it. Conditional Access policies decide when to allow, block, or challenge sign-ins based on conditions such as location, device health, and risk level. Identity Protection uses machine learning to detect risky sign-ins and compromised accounts, and governance tools handle access reviews, entitlement management, and privileged access. It extends to customers and partners through external identity features, and increasingly to non-human identities such as apps and AI agents.

item.title: Microsoft Security Copilot
item.description:
Security Copilot aims to relieve the pressure on overstretched security operations teams. An analyst can ask in plain language what happened in an incident, and Copilot gathers signals from Microsoft’s security products, summarizes the attack path, explains the alerts, and suggests next steps. It can write queries in languages like KQL, analyze suspicious scripts and files, and produce incident reports, saving time on routine tasks.

The product has moved toward agents. Purpose-built agents handle jobs such as triaging phishing alerts, assessing vulnerabilities, and prioritizing conditions that need attention, working with human oversight. It is embedded in the portals analysts already use, and plugins connect to non-Microsoft tools, so it can use data from other systems. Controls govern what it can access and do.

item.title: Motive
item.description:
Motive started as KeepTruckin with electronic logging devices that record drivers’ hours, which US regulations require for many commercial trucks. It expanded into a fleet platform with GPS tracking, vehicle diagnostics, and tools for compliance, dispatching, and maintenance, serving trucking companies, construction firms, and other businesses with vehicles on the road.

AI dashcams are a major product. A camera facing the road and the driver uses computer vision to detect events such as distracted driving, phone use, following too closely, and rolling stops, and alerts drivers in real time while sending clips to managers for coaching. Safety scoring, reports, and exoneration video after accidents help reduce incidents and insurance costs. The company also offers a fleet card and spend controls.

item.title: MX
item.description:
MX is a financial data platform. It gathers account and transaction data from thousands of institutions, enriches it by cleaning merchant names and categorizing spending, and delivers it to banks, credit unions, and fintech apps that want to offer money management features.

Its products include account aggregation, a digital banking experience that institutions can embed, insights and budgeting tools, and data for lending decisions. AI improves categorization and personalization, and connections increasingly use direct bank APIs instead of screen scraping.

item.title: Nansen
item.description:
Nansen turns raw blockchain data into readable information. Every wallet on a public chain is an anonymous string of characters, so Nansen builds a database of labels, tagging wallets that belong to exchanges, funds, protocols, and traders with a track record. Seeing that a labeled fund bought a token is more informative than seeing an unknown address.

Dashboards track token flows, new token launches, NFT activity, and the holdings of tagged wallets. Alerts notify users when watched wallets move funds, and analytical tools help researchers study a project’s holders and trading patterns. An AI assistant answers questions about on-chain data in plain language, and it supports many chains.

item.title: OpenSolar
item.description:
OpenSolar helps solar installers and sales teams win jobs. A user enters an address, and the software pulls satellite imagery and builds a 3D model of the roof, where panels can be placed and shading analyzed. It estimates energy production and savings, then generates a proposal customers can view online and sign.

The platform includes tools for the whole sales process. A customer relationship manager tracks leads, a pricing engine builds quotes, and integrated financing lets homeowners compare loan or lease options. AI features automate roof detection and layout, which speeds up design for each prospect, and electrical design tools help with permit packages.

item.title: OrcaSlicer
item.description:
OrcaSlicer prepares 3D models for printing. It loads a model, lets you orient it and add supports, then generates the toolpaths that tell the printer what to do. It grew out of Bambu Studio and Slic3r-family projects and has become popular because it offers many settings alongside sensible defaults.

Calibration is a standout feature. Built-in tests help tune flow rate, pressure advance, temperature, and retraction for each filament, which improves quality and consistency. It supports many printers through profiles, manages multiple materials and colors, and can send jobs to printers over a network.

item.title: Oura Ring
item.description:
Oura packs sensors into a ring that is comfortable to wear day and night. It tracks sleep stages, resting heart rate, heart rate variability, body temperature, and movement, then gives scores for sleep and readiness that suggest how hard to push each day. Many people choose it for sleep tracking, since a ring is less obtrusive than a watch in bed, and battery life lasts several days.

The app presents trends and offers guidance. Features cover cycle and fertility insights, stress and recovery information, activity goals, and workouts. An AI advisor lets users ask questions about their data in plain language and receive personalized suggestions. Oura works with Apple Health, Google Health Connect, and other apps, and it has partnered with companies in areas like glucose monitoring.

item.title: Percy
item.description:
Percy automates visual testing. Developers add it to their test suite, and on each code change it captures screenshots of pages and components across browsers and screen sizes. It compares them with an approved baseline and highlights the pixels that differ, so a reviewer can accept intended changes or catch accidental ones before they reach users.

Visual bugs, such as overlapping text, broken layouts, or missing images, often slip past functional tests, which only check behavior. Percy fills this gap and integrates with pull requests, so design and engineering can review changes together. AI helps ignore noise like anti-aliasing differences or dynamic content, which keeps the review list short.

item.title: Physical Intelligence
item.description:
Physical Intelligence works on foundation models for robots. Most robots are programmed for one job, but the company aims to train a general model that can control many kinds of robots to do many tasks, such as folding laundry, clearing tables, and packing items, by learning from large amounts of robot data.

It has released research and open models, including the pi-zero family of vision-language-action models, along with code that lets other researchers try them. These models take camera images and instructions in natural language and output actions for the robot. The company collaborates with robot makers and collects data across different hardware.

item.title: QGIS
item.description:
QGIS gives anyone access to professional-level mapping and spatial analysis at no cost. Users load vector and raster data from files, databases, and web services, style maps, edit geometries, and run analyses such as buffers, overlays, terrain analysis, and routing. A processing toolbox bundles hundreds of algorithms, and it integrates with GRASS and SAGA for specialized tasks. It handles many formats and projections, and print layouts produce publication-quality maps.

The plugin ecosystem is a major strength. Community-developed plugins add functions for data download, cartography, hydrology, field data collection, and more, and Python scripting supports automation. In AI-related work, plugins bring in machine learning for tasks like classifying land cover, detecting objects in imagery, and using models such as Segment Anything for segmentation. Users run QGIS Server to publish maps and QField to collect data on mobile devices.

item.title: Qualio
item.description:
Qualio is designed for regulated life sciences companies that need a quality system but not a heavy enterprise one. Teams write and approve controlled documents, assign and track training, manage change requests and corrective actions, and keep the records auditors expect, all in a cloud app with electronic signatures.

The product is aimed at smaller and growth-stage companies. Pre-built templates and workflows speed up setup, and the platform adds modules for events, risk, and supplier qualification. AI features help draft and review documents and answer questions about the quality system.

item.title: Questel
item.description:
Questel serves people who work with patents and trademarks. Its search tools let users query large databases of patents from many countries, apply classifications, and find prior art for patentability and infringement questions. Analytics show landscapes of who is filing in a field and trends over time.

The company also offers portfolio management, with docketing, renewals, and workflow tools for tracking deadlines across jurisdictions, along with services for filing and annuity payments. AI features assist with semantic search, summarization, and drafting, helping professionals review large numbers of documents faster. Its products come from combining several IP software companies.

item.title: QuickBooks
item.description: QuickBooks is the accounting software most small businesses and their accountants know. QuickBooks Online runs in a browser and on phones, connects to bank accounts to import transactions, sends invoices, tracks bills and expenses, and produces profit and loss statements, balance sheets, and cash flow reports. It also supports sales tax tracking, inventory in higher tiers, and multi-user access for bookkeepers and accountants. A desktop edition remains for businesses that prefer installed software.

item.title: QuickNode
item.description:
QuickNode offers blockchain infrastructure as a service. Running a node for a blockchain takes hardware, storage, and maintenance, so QuickNode hosts them and gives developers endpoints they connect to over standard protocols. Apps use these endpoints to fetch balances, read smart contract data, and submit transactions.

Beyond basic access, the platform includes tools for data and automation. Add-ons offer token and NFT APIs, streaming of on-chain events, and workflows that move blockchain data into databases. It supports many networks, including Ethereum, Solana, and layer 2 chains, with dashboards for usage and performance monitoring.

item.title: Qure.ai
item.description:
Qure.ai makes AI tools for radiology. Its software reads medical images and highlights suspected abnormalities, such as signs of tuberculosis or pneumonia on a chest X-ray, or a hemorrhage on a head CT. The software returns an annotated image and a short summary, so radiologists and clinicians can prioritize urgent cases.

The company is known for working in settings with few radiologists. Screening programs for tuberculosis use its tools to triage chest X-rays quickly, and hospitals use it to speed up emergency reads. It has regulatory clearances in several markets and integrates with PACS systems, the software that stores and displays medical images.

item.title: Rasa
item.description:
Rasa is a toolkit for developers who build conversational assistants. It started with machine learning components for understanding user messages and managing dialogue, and has evolved to combine language models with structured business logic. Teams define flows for tasks such as updating an address or booking an appointment, and the model handles the language.

Control is its main appeal. Companies can host Rasa themselves, keeping conversations and customer data within their own environment, and decide exactly what the assistant is allowed to do. That suits banks, telecoms, and healthcare organizations with strict privacy and compliance needs, and it reduces the risk of a language model improvising.

item.title: Rask AI
item.description:
Rask AI makes video localization simpler. You upload a video or provide a link, and the tool transcribes the speech, translates it into one of many languages, and produces a new audio track with a synthetic voice. Editing tools let you correct the transcript and translation before generating the final version.

Additional features improve the result. Voice cloning keeps the speaker’s voice character in the new language, and lip sync adjusts the mouth movements to match the dubbed audio. It also handles multiple speakers, subtitles, and exports, and offers an API for teams that localize at scale.

item.title: ReadMe
item.description:
ReadMe helps companies document their APIs. Teams upload an OpenAPI specification, and the platform generates an interactive reference with code samples in several languages and a try-it console that makes real requests with the reader’s own key. Guides and changelogs sit alongside, forming a single developer hub.

It is also a source of insight. API owners see which endpoints developers use, where requests fail, and which pages cause confusion, so documentation can improve based on evidence. Personalized docs show a logged-in developer their own API keys and data, which makes onboarding faster. An AI assistant answers questions from the documentation.

item.title: RoseTTAFold
item.description:
RoseTTAFold predicts how a chain of amino acids folds into a three-dimensional protein. Knowing a protein’s shape helps scientists understand what it does and how to target it with drugs. The model was developed at the Institute for Protein Design and the University of Washington, around the same time as AlphaFold, and offered a comparable approach with a three-track neural network.

The work has grown into a family. RoseTTAFold All-Atom models complexes that include small molecules, DNA, and other components, and RFdiffusion generates new protein backbones for design tasks such as binders and enzymes. Together these tools support a shift from predicting existing proteins to creating new ones, with applications in medicine and materials.

item.title: Sardine
item.description:
Sardine is a fraud and compliance platform for financial services. It collects signals about the device and the way a user interacts, such as typing patterns and whether a session looks automated, and combines them with transaction data to score the risk of an account opening, a payment, or a login. Decisions happen in milliseconds, so legitimate customers face little friction.

The platform covers a range of risk. It addresses account takeover, payment fraud, scams, and identity fraud, and integrates with know your customer and anti-money laundering workflows. AI agents help compliance teams by gathering evidence, reviewing alerts, and drafting case notes, which reduces the manual work behind investigations.

item.title: Secureframe
item.description:
Secureframe automates compliance work. It integrates with cloud providers, code repositories, identity systems, and HR tools to check that required controls are in place, gather evidence for auditors, and alert teams when something drifts out of compliance.

The platform also manages policies, employee training, vendor risk, and a trust page for customers. AI drafts policies, maps controls across frameworks, and fills in security questionnaires from a company’s own answers, saving time during sales cycles.

item.title: Securiti
item.description:
Securiti addresses the problem that companies often do not know where their sensitive data lives. It scans cloud storage, databases, SaaS apps, and data pipelines, classifies personal and confidential information, and builds a map of where it sits and who can access it. This approach is known as data security posture management.

On top of that, it automates privacy and governance tasks. Teams respond to data subject requests, manage consent, run privacy assessments, and enforce policies that block risky access. For AI, Securiti helps discover models and data feeding them, apply guardrails, and meet emerging regulations, which has become a priority as companies adopt generative AI.

item.title: Seeing AI
item.description:
Seeing AI turns a smartphone into a talking camera. Point it at printed text and it reads aloud, short text instantly or whole documents with guidance for framing the page. It recognizes products by scanning barcodes, identifies currency notes, describes colors, and detects light levels, helping with everyday tasks like finding the right can in a pantry.

More advanced channels describe scenes and people. The app can give a description of a photo or surroundings, recognize friends who have been added with consent, and describe their apparent expressions. Handwriting reading and image exploration by touch are available on supported devices, and newer versions use generative AI to give more detailed descriptions and answer follow-up questions.

item.title: SentinelOne
item.description:
SentinelOne is a cybersecurity company known for autonomous endpoint protection. Its agent runs on computers and servers, uses machine learning to detect malicious behavior on the device, and can respond automatically by isolating a machine, killing a process, or rolling back changes made by ransomware. That local decision-making works even when a device is offline.

The Singularity platform extends this across the environment. It brings together endpoint detection and response with cloud workload security, identity threat detection, vulnerability management, and a data lake that collects logs from many sources for threat hunting. Purple AI is a generative assistant that lets analysts ask questions in natural language, such as whether a suspicious file appeared elsewhere, and turns them into queries, summarizes findings, and suggests next steps.

item.title: Shortform
item.description:
Shortform sits between a short summary and the book itself. Each guide covers a book’s ideas in depth, adds analysis comparing it with other books, and includes exercises that help readers apply the lessons. Readers can use them to decide what to read in full or to review a book they have finished.

The library spans business, psychology, history, and self-help, and includes guides to classic works and some articles and fiction. AI features offer a chat assistant for asking questions about a guide.

item.title: SnapGene
item.description:
SnapGene gives molecular biologists a visual, reliable way to plan DNA work. Researchers open or create plasmid and DNA sequences, see features such as genes and promoters automatically annotated, and simulate cloning steps like restriction digests, ligations, Gibson assembly, and Gateway cloning before going to the bench. The tool shows resulting maps and sequences, helping avoid costly mistakes.

It has a large library of standard vectors and features, tools for designing primers, and a viewer that lets collaborators open files without a license. Sequence comparison, alignments, and the ability to import from databases support daily lab tasks. Files are shared in a format that is widely used across the field. A server version supports team libraries.

item.title: Snorkel AI
item.description:
Snorkel started as an academic project that asked whether people could label data programmatically. Instead of tagging thousands of examples one by one, a domain expert writes labeling functions, which are rules, patterns, or model calls that vote on a label. Snorkel combines their noisy outputs into training labels, a technique called weak supervision.

The company has moved toward the needs of generative AI. Its platform helps enterprises curate data for fine-tuning and evaluating language models, with experts reviewing samples and defining what good answers look like. A network of expert annotators supplies specialized data in areas like law, medicine, and finance, and tools measure how models perform on custom benchmarks.

item.title: Splunk
item.description:
Splunk made machine data searchable. It ingests logs, metrics, and events from servers, applications, networks, and cloud services, indexes them, and lets users search and visualize with its Search Processing Language. Companies use it to troubleshoot outages, monitor performance, and investigate security incidents, and it has been a mainstay of security operations centers for many years.

The product line includes Splunk Enterprise and Splunk Cloud for core analytics, Enterprise Security as a SIEM for threat detection, and observability tools for infrastructure and application monitoring. AI features include an assistant that helps write searches from plain language and summarizes findings, and machine learning for anomaly detection. Cisco acquired Splunk and is integrating it with its networking and security products.

item.title: Storytel
item.description:
Storytel gives readers and listeners unlimited access to a library through a monthly subscription. The company began in Sweden and is a major audiobook service across the Nordics, with strong local-language catalogs in many markets, including Spanish, Polish, and Indian languages. Listeners use the mobile app to stream or download books and can adjust speed and set sleep timers.

The service has experimented with AI. VoiceSwitcher lets a listener change between the original human narrator and a synthetic voice for the same book, which helps with books that would not otherwise be recorded. Storytel also uses AI voices to expand its catalog and to translate books, an approach that has drawn debate about the role of human narrators.

item.title: Sumsub
item.description:
Sumsub provides identity verification for online services that must know who their customers are. A user photographs an ID document and takes a selfie, and Sumsub checks that the document is real, matches the person, and that a live person is present, which helps block stolen identities and deepfakes. Results come back in seconds or minutes.

Beyond onboarding, the platform covers compliance. It screens users against sanctions and politically exposed persons lists, monitors transactions for suspicious behavior, and supports business verification for companies. Fraud prevention features detect fake documents, duplicate accounts, and bots, and a case management dashboard lets compliance staff review flagged applicants.

item.title: Surge AI
item.description:
Surge AI supplies the human judgment that goes into modern language models. Labs need people to compare answers, write ideal responses, and grade quality, and these ratings train models through techniques like RLHF. Surge recruits and manages annotators with specialized skills, such as coding, writing, and expertise in science, law, or medicine.

Its pitch is quality over crowd volume. Careful screening, training, and quality checks aim to produce data that is more accurate than what general crowd platforms deliver. Services include building evaluation sets, adversarial testing to find model weaknesses, and custom datasets for specific tasks. The company works with large AI developers and publishes research on data quality.

item.title: Talkspace
item.description:
Talkspace lets people get mental health care remotely. Users complete an assessment, are matched with a licensed therapist, and can communicate through messaging, live video, or audio sessions, which makes treatment convenient and sometimes more affordable than in-person visits. Psychiatry services provide evaluations and medication management where appropriate.

A major difference from some competitors is insurance coverage: many users can pay with commercial insurance or Medicare plans through Talkspace, and employers and health plans offer it as a benefit. The company has added AI tools for matching, documentation, and safety monitoring, and is exploring ways AI can support providers while keeping therapy human. It publishes research on outcomes.

item.title: The Batch
item.description: The Batch is a free weekly newsletter for people who follow AI. Each issue begins with a letter from Andrew Ng, a leading AI researcher and educator, sharing his perspective on a current topic, such as how teams should build with AI or what trends matter. That is followed by several concise news items on research, products, policy, and industry developments, each with a clear explanation and links to sources.

item.title: Tinder
item.description: Tinder popularized the swipe. You see a profile with photos and a short bio, swipe right to like or left to pass, and if the other person also likes you, you match and can message. The format is fast and casual, which fits its large, young user base across many countries. People use it for dating, relationships, and meeting new people, and settings let you filter by distance, age, and gender preferences.

item.title: TLDR AI
item.description:
TLDR AI is a quick daily read for people who work with or follow AI. Each issue lists a handful of top stories, such as model releases, research papers, tools, and industry news, with a two- or three-sentence summary and a link to the full source. The format is meant to be read in a few minutes, so subscribers can stay current without sifting through feeds.

It belongs to a family of TLDR newsletters covering tech, startups, and other fields. The AI edition includes sections for headlines, research, engineering and open-source projects, and miscellaneous items, with reading times shown so readers can choose what to open. It is supported by sponsorships, which are labeled.

item.title: Tractive
item.description:
Tractive helps owners keep track of their pets. A small GPS device attached to a collar sends the animal’s location to a phone app via cellular networks, so you can see where your dog or cat is in real time, view recent routes, and set virtual fences that trigger alerts if the pet leaves a defined area. A light and sound function helps find a pet at night.

Beyond location, the devices monitor activity, sleep, and behavior, and some models track signs of health changes such as excessive scratching or licking. Data shows trends and can help owners share information with veterinarians. Features such as a lost-pet mode, sharing access with family, and integration with pet services support everyday use.

item.title: Trimble Construction
item.description:
Trimble is a major technology supplier to the construction industry. Its portfolio includes software for estimating costs, scheduling, managing projects and finances, coordinating building models, and running equipment. SketchUp and Tekla, used for design and structural detailing, are part of the group, and Trimble Connect provides a collaboration space for project data.

Its hardware is a distinctive strength. Survey instruments, GPS and GNSS receivers, and machine control systems guide excavators and other equipment based on a 3D model, linking digital plans to work on the ground. Integrating these systems with software lets data flow from the model to the field and back as built information. AI features assist with planning, quantity takeoff, and analyzing project data.

item.title: Upstart
item.description:
Upstart set out to improve how lenders decide who gets credit. Its models use many variables, including education, job history, and credit data, to predict the likelihood a borrower will repay, with the aim of approving more people at lower rates than traditional scores alone would. Borrowers apply online, often receive decisions quickly, and loans are funded by partner banks and credit unions.

The platform serves lenders as software and as a marketplace. Banks use Upstart to originate personal loans, auto loans, and home equity products, with automation that speeds approvals and reduces manual review. The company regularly tests its models for disparate impact, and has worked with regulators on fair lending, which remains a major concern for AI in credit.

item.title: UserWay
item.description:
UserWay is a web accessibility service. Its widget gives visitors controls to adjust text size, contrast, spacing, and animations, and it applies automated fixes such as adding missing labels. A scanner checks pages against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines and reports issues, so site owners can see problems and prioritize them.

For deeper work, UserWay offers managed services with human experts who audit and fix content, plus tools for documents and PDFs. Reports and accessibility statements help show good faith efforts toward compliance. The product works with common platforms such as WordPress, Shopify, and Wix.

item.title: Vertex
item.description:
Vertex helps businesses get sales and use tax, VAT, and similar indirect taxes right. When a company sells a product, the right tax depends on the buyer’s location, the product type, and applicable rules, which change often. Vertex maintains a large database of rates and rules, and its engine calculates the correct tax inside systems like SAP, Oracle, and Microsoft Dynamics.

The company also covers filing and reporting. Tools prepare returns, manage exemption certificates, and support e-invoicing mandates that countries are introducing. AI features help classify products to the right tax codes and speed up compliance work. Customers are mostly large enterprises with complex tax footprints across many jurisdictions.

item.title: Vuforia
item.description:
Vuforia is one of the longest-running AR toolkits. Developers use its engine to make an app recognize a printed image, a 3D object, or a physical space, and then anchor digital content to it. A technician could point a tablet at a machine and see step-by-step instructions overlaid on the right parts.

PTC has focused it on industry. Vuforia products include tools for creating work instructions, remote expert assistance with live video and annotations, and authoring tools that turn CAD models into AR experiences without much coding. It supports phones, tablets, and headsets, and connects to PTC’s engineering software.

item.title: Winston AI
item.description:
Winston AI is a detection tool for written content. A user pastes text or uploads a document, and the service returns a score estimating how likely it is that AI wrote it, with sentence-level highlighting. A plagiarism checker compares text against web sources, and reports can be shared as evidence.

Publishers use it to screen submissions, teachers to review student work, and agencies to check freelancers. Additional features include detection of AI-generated images and tools aimed at checking whether text has been paraphrased to evade detection. Browser extensions and an API support workflows.

item.title: Wisdom Panel
item.description:
Wisdom Panel offers genetic testing for dogs and cats. An owner swabs the pet’s cheek, mails the sample, and receives a report on breed ancestry, family tree, and traits. The report also screens for genetic health conditions the pet may carry or be at risk for, which can inform decisions with a veterinarian.

The company draws on a large database of breed samples and research, and sells tests through retailers, directly to owners, and through veterinary clinics. Health screening results are meant to start conversations with a vet, and some conditions come with guidance on diet or monitoring. The brand belongs to Mars Petcare, which also owns other pet care businesses.

item.title: Xero
item.description:
Xero is an online accounting platform used widely in the UK, Australia, New Zealand, and increasingly elsewhere. Business owners and bookkeepers connect their bank accounts so transactions flow in automatically, then match them to invoices and bills in a reconciliation process that Xero makes quick with suggested matches. It generates invoices, tracks expenses and cash flow, and produces reports such as profit and loss and balance sheets.

An accountant-friendly design is part of its appeal. Unlimited users on most plans let owners, bookkeepers, and accountants work in the same file, and a large marketplace of integrations connects Xero to payment providers, payroll, inventory, and point-of-sale systems. AI features include suggested coding of transactions, predictive cash flow tools, and an assistant for asking questions about the business and automating tasks like drafting invoice reminders.

item.title: Aquant
item.description:
Aquant is a service intelligence platform. Equipment makers and service organizations hold years of repair history, manuals, and technician notes, which are hard to search in the moment. Aquant uses AI to learn from that data and recommend probable causes and fixes for a given symptom.

For a technician on a job, this works like an expert on call. They describe the problem or enter an error code, and the system suggests what to check, which parts are likely needed, and what has worked on similar cases. Service managers use the same data to see recurring failures and to reduce repeat visits and unnecessary parts.

item.title: AspenTech
item.description:
AspenTech sells engineering software to process industries. Chemical engineers use Aspen Plus and Aspen HYSYS to model how reactions, separations, and heat flows behave across a plant, which lets them design and test processes on screen before building them, and tune existing plants for efficiency, safety, and emissions.

The company also sells operations software. Optimization tools help plants decide how to run units to hit targets for cost and throughput, and asset performance products use machine learning on sensor data to predict equipment failures before they cause downtime. Digital twins of plant units connect design models to real operating data.

item.title: Bluebeam
item.description:
Bluebeam Revu is a PDF tool built for construction. Teams review plans on screen, add markups such as clouds, callouts, and stamps, and measure lengths, areas, and counts directly on drawings to prepare quantity takeoffs for estimates. Custom tool sets store commonly used markups.

Collaboration is a big part. Studio Sessions let many people mark up the same document at the same time, and Studio Projects store drawing sets in the cloud. Overlay and comparison features show what changed between revisions, with AI helping to line up sheets and highlight differences, which reduces missed updates.

item.title: Buildertrend
item.description:
Buildertrend focuses on residential construction. Builders manage a project from estimate to completion in a single system: schedules, selections, budgets, purchase orders, daily logs, photos, and documents. Clients can log in to approve choices, view progress, and see invoices, which cuts down on phone calls.

Financial tools track costs against budgets, handle change orders, and send bills and payments. Subcontractors get access to their schedules and tasks, and mobile apps let teams update from the job site. AI features assist with tasks like summarizing communication and extracting data from documents.

item.title: CAST AI
item.description:
CAST AI is an automation layer for Kubernetes. After connecting to a cluster on AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure, it analyzes workloads, chooses the best-priced instance types, scales nodes up and down, and replaces expensive capacity with spot instances when workloads can tolerate interruptions.

The platform also covers related needs. Savings reports show the effect, workload autoscaling adjusts resource requests, and security scanning finds misconfigurations. More recently it added tools for running GPU workloads and AI inference more efficiently. Customers keep their own cloud accounts.

item.title: Cognite
item.description:
Cognite addresses data silos in industry. A plant produces time series from sensors, maintenance records, engineering diagrams, and 3D models that live in different systems. Cognite Data Fusion links them into a graph in which a pump, its sensor readings, its work orders, and its drawings are connected, so people and applications can find everything about an asset.

That foundation supports applications. Teams build digital twins, predictive maintenance models, and dashboards, and an AI assistant helps users ask questions about assets and operations in natural language. The platform is used in oil and gas, power, and manufacturing, where downtime is costly.

item.title: ComplyAdvantage
item.description:
ComplyAdvantage provides financial crime tools for banks, fintechs, and other regulated firms. At onboarding, it checks whether a customer or company appears on sanctions lists, politically exposed person lists, or negative news, and continues to monitor them over time. Transaction monitoring flags unusual activity that may signal money laundering.

Its data comes from a large collection of sources that is structured and updated continuously, and machine learning ranks matches to cut down on false alarms that compliance staff would otherwise review by hand. Case management tools help analysts document decisions for regulators, and risk assessment features support a risk-based approach.

item.title: Datarock
item.description:
Datarock works in mineral exploration. Geologists take photos of drill core samples and log what they see, which is slow and subjective. Datarock’s models analyze the images to identify rock types, measure fractures, and capture structural features, producing consistent digital logs.

The faster, more objective data helps exploration teams make decisions about where to drill next and supports resource modeling. Results integrate with geological software, and the company has expanded to other imagery such as hyperspectral scans and borehole images.

item.title: Dental Monitoring
item.description:
Dental Monitoring lets orthodontists check on patients remotely. A patient attaches a small cheek retractor to a phone, scans their teeth on a schedule, and uploads the images. The software compares scans to the treatment plan and measures how teeth are moving.

AI flags problems such as aligners that do not fit, lost attachments, hygiene concerns, or progress that is behind schedule. The orthodontist reviews alerts and decides whether to adjust the plan, send the next aligners earlier, or schedule a visit. This can reduce in-person appointments and catch issues sooner.

item.title: Edge Impulse
item.description:
Edge Impulse brings machine learning to small devices. An engineer collects data from sensors such as accelerometers, microphones, and cameras, labels it, designs a processing pipeline, trains a model in the browser, and exports an optimized version that runs on a microcontroller or edge processor. Applications include detecting equipment faults, recognizing keywords, and spotting objects.

The platform supports a wide range of hardware and shows estimates of memory use and latency before deployment, which matters when resources are tiny. Tools help with data collection and testing, and integrations connect to major chip vendors. Qualcomm acquired the company to strengthen its edge AI offering.

item.title: Eyenuk
item.description:
Eyenuk focuses on automated eye screening. A technician captures retinal images with a compatible camera, and EyeArt analyzes them and reports whether signs of more-than-mild disease are present, flagging patients who need referral. The process takes about a minute and does not need a specialist to read the images.

The purpose is to expand screening for people with diabetes who miss annual eye exams. Primary care clinics, endocrinology practices, and optometrists use it to catch disease earlier. The company has expanded the technology to other conditions and offers versions for different clinical settings.

item.title: ForeFlight
item.description:
ForeFlight is an app for planning and flying. Pilots build routes, check weather and airspace, file flight plans, and view approach plates and charts. In the air, it shows moving maps and traffic and weather from compatible receivers, which replaces paper charts.

Weather is a big part. Layers show forecasts, radar, and hazards, and tools highlight conditions most likely to affect a given route. Performance and weight and balance planning help with safety, and integrations connect to avionics and tablets. Teams in flight departments use it to share data.

item.title: Greenlight Guru
item.description:
Greenlight Guru serves a heavily regulated industry. Medical device makers must document how a product was designed, how risks were assessed, and how problems are corrected. The platform organizes these records, links requirements to risks and tests, and keeps them audit ready, replacing documents scattered in shared drives.

Modules cover design controls, risk management, document control, training, supplier management, and corrective and preventive actions. AI features help draft documents and risk analyses and answer questions about regulations, saving time on repetitive writing. A clinical module supports post-market work.

item.title: Instrumentl
item.description:
Instrumentl is a grant discovery and management platform. A nonprofit describes its mission and programs, and the system recommends foundation and government grants that fit, with details on the funder’s giving history, typical award sizes, and past recipients. Alerts notify the team when new matches appear.

Once a grant is identified, a tracker handles tasks, deadlines, reports, and documents for each application, with collaboration for the team. AI assists with research, summarizing funder priorities and drafting parts of proposals, though grant writing still depends on strong program knowledge.

item.title: Keela
item.description:
Keela helps small and mid-sized nonprofits manage supporters. It keeps donor records, gifts, and communication history, processes online donations, runs email campaigns, and supports events and volunteer tracking. The platform aims to be affordable and approachable for teams without a dedicated data staff.

AI features guide outreach. Engagement scoring highlights supporters likely to give again or increase gifts, timing suggestions prompt contact when it is most effective, and a writing assistant drafts appeals and thank-you notes. Reports show campaign results and giving trends.

item.title: Kentik
item.description:
Kentik gives network teams insight into how traffic moves. It collects flow records, routing information, and metrics from routers, switches, and cloud networks, stores them at large scale, and lets engineers query who is talking to whom and how much. That helps with capacity planning, troubleshooting, and cost control.

Security and reliability uses include detecting DDoS attacks and unusual traffic patterns, analyzing BGP routing changes, and finding the reason for a slowdown across multiple networks. An AI assistant lets users ask questions in plain language and speeds up root cause analysis. Cloud and data center networks are covered.

item.title: Mentalyc
item.description:
Mentalyc is an AI note-taking tool for mental health professionals. A therapist records a session, uploads audio, or enters brief notes, and the tool generates a structured progress note that matches the format their practice uses. The clinician edits and approves it.

The product emphasizes privacy, since therapy content is sensitive. It states that it follows health privacy rules and offers controls such as removing identifying details. It also supports treatment plans and can learn a therapist’s style over time.

item.title: Notarize (Proof)
item.description:
Notarize brought notarization online. A signer uploads a document, verifies identity by scanning an ID and answering questions, joins a video call with a commissioned notary, and signs digitally. The notary applies a digital seal and the document is stored securely, making a process that required an in-person visit possible from home.

The company, now operating as Proof, expanded into broader identity and signature products for businesses, including title and escrow, banks, and real estate. AI-based checks examine ID documents and confirm that a live person is present, which helps resist fraud.

item.title: Propeller Aero
item.description:
Propeller serves construction, mining, and quarry sites. A drone flies a site, often with ground control targets, and the images are processed into accurate maps and 3D models. Users measure stockpiles, cut and fill volumes, and compare the site with design plans.

Dashboards share progress with project teams, and tools track haul roads, compare surveys over time, and generate reports for clients. Its PPK-enabled hardware and workflow aim to improve accuracy and reduce the need for ground control points.

item.title: Shift Technology
item.description:
Shift Technology serves insurers. When a claim arrives, its models assess the likelihood of fraud, explain the red flags, and route the case, so investigators spend time on the suspicious ones while clean claims are paid quickly.

The company extends the approach to underwriting, subrogation, and customer service, and has added generative AI agents that help adjusters summarize files and handle routine tasks. Its customers include large carriers around the world.

item.title: Smartify
item.description:
Smartify is an app for cultural venues. A visitor opens it in a partner museum, scans an artwork with the camera, and the app identifies it and shows background, artist information, and audio commentary. Collections can be saved for later.

Museums use it to enrich visits without installing hardware, and to learn what visitors engage with. The platform includes tools for creating tours and for accessibility. Some partners are major institutions.

item.title: Tracers
item.description:
Tracers is an investigative data service. A user enters a name, address, or other identifier, and the platform returns linked records about people and businesses, such as addresses, relatives, liens, and court filings. Matching algorithms connect pieces of information.

Customers include private investigators, attorneys, collections agencies, and law enforcement. Access is restricted by law in many cases and requires a permissible purpose, and results have limits in accuracy.

Tracers is sold on subscription and per search. Using such data raises privacy and legal issues, and background checks used for employment or housing are subject to consumer reporting laws. Alternatives include LexisNexis Accurint, TLOxp, Thomson Reuters CLEAR, and IRB Search. Tracers suits licensed investigative professionals.

item.title: Tractable
item.description:
Tractable applies computer vision to insurance claims. After an accident, a policyholder or repairer uploads photos, and the AI identifies damaged parts and estimates repair costs, speeding up decisions that used to wait for an inspection.

Insurers use it to settle simple claims fast, to triage complex ones, and to detect inconsistencies. The company has expanded to property damage after disasters and to the used-parts and repair industries.

Tractable is sold to insurers and repair networks on enterprise contracts. Automated estimates affect people’s payments, so fairness, accuracy, and appeal routes matter. Alternatives include CCC Intelligent Solutions, Solera, Mitchell, Shift Technology, and Cambridge Mobile Telematics. Tractable suits insurers speeding up claims.

item.title: Upheal
item.description:
Upheal helps therapists reduce paperwork. With client consent, the tool records or transcribes a session and drafts a note in the clinician’s preferred format, which they review and sign. It can summarize progress over time and suggest treatment plan updates.

The product emphasizes privacy and compliance with health data rules, and offers a free tier for solo practitioners. Session insights, such as talk time and themes, give feedback to the clinician.

item.title: Wildbook
item.description:
Wildbook turns photos into population data. Scientists and citizen scientists upload pictures of animals such as whale sharks, giraffes, and sea turtles, and the software recognizes individuals by distinctive markings, such as spot patterns or fin shapes, and links sightings over time.

That reveals movement, survival, and population size without physically tagging animals. The platform supports many species, with separate databases for each, and photos from tourists and social media can contribute.

item.title: Cuey
item.description:
Cuey is a tool for comparing chatbots. From a sidebar in Chrome, you type a prompt once and it goes to services such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini that you are logged into, with the responses displayed together. A view highlights where the answers agree and differ, which is useful for fact-checking and choosing the best phrasing.

It includes a library of saved prompts and a memory feature so context can follow you from one model to another. Because it works with the chat interfaces you already use, it does not need separate API keys. The developer, Llama Valley Inc, states that prompts and responses are not stored on its servers.
