Companies in logistics, travel, real estate, and mobility use it to show routes, locations, and live data.

The platform goes beyond display. APIs handle geocoding and search, turn-by-turn navigation, route optimization, isochrones that show how far you can get in a given time, and traffic-aware directions. A navigation SDK supports in-app guidance, and tools for working with large geospatial datasets allow analysis and visualization. Machine learning is used for features such as map matching and road data updates, and recent products add AI assistants for developers.

item.title: Maxar Technologies
item.description:
Maxar was best known for high-resolution satellite imagery. Its WorldView satellites photographed the Earth in great detail, and governments, news organizations, mapmakers, and businesses used the images for defense and intelligence, disaster response, agriculture, infrastructure monitoring, and navigation. Maxar’s imagery supported mapping products and was often seen in news coverage of conflicts and natural disasters.

Its other major business was space systems: building satellites and spacecraft components for communications, observation, and exploration. Machine learning was applied to extract features such as buildings, roads, and vehicles from imagery at scale, and to create 3D models of the Earth. The company was taken private by a private equity firm and later separated its two main businesses under new names.

item.title: Mermaid Chart
item.description:
Mermaid is a popular open-source way to create diagrams by writing text. You describe a flowchart or sequence diagram in a few lines of code, and it renders as a graphic, which makes diagrams easy to version in Git, embed in documentation, and update alongside code. GitHub, GitLab, and many documentation tools render Mermaid natively, and developers like that diagrams stay in plain text.

Mermaid Chart is the company and product founded by the creator of Mermaid. It provides a web editor with live preview, a visual drag-and-drop editor for people who prefer not to write code, templates, and collaboration features such as sharing and comments. AI can generate diagrams from a description, fix syntax errors, and suggest changes, which lowers the barrier for beginners. Plugins integrate with VS Code, Confluence, Jira, and other tools.

item.title: Meta Quest
item.description:
Meta Quest headsets made virtual reality mainstream by removing the need for cables and a powerful computer. The headsets have built-in processors, controllers, and cameras that track your hands and surroundings, and run apps from the Quest store. The latest models support mixed reality, blending virtual objects with the live view of the room, which opens up games and tools that interact with your space.

The ecosystem includes a wide range of experiences. Popular uses include games, fitness apps, social worlds, watching videos on virtual screens, and creating or collaborating in 3D. Meta is adding AI features, including Meta AI as a voice assistant and tools that help creators build worlds, and headsets can connect to a PC for more demanding games. Models vary in price and capability, and the software is called Horizon OS.

item.title: MindMeister
item.description:
MindMeister helps you think in branches. You start with a central topic and add connected ideas around it, using keyboard shortcuts to build a map quickly. Maps can be formatted with colors, icons, images, links, and notes, rearranged freely, and turned into outlines. People use it for brainstorming, studying, project planning, meeting notes, and mapping out content such as articles or courses.

Collaboration is a core strength. Several people can edit a map at once, with comments and voting to gather input, and maps can be shared by link. A presentation mode turns a map into slides, and tasks can be assigned on map nodes and synced with the project tools in the same suite. Integrations connect with Google Workspace, Microsoft Teams, and other apps, and exports include PDF, image, and Word formats. AI features suggest ideas and generate map structures from a topic.

item.title: Moralis
item.description:
Moralis provides ready-made APIs for blockchain data. Instead of reading raw blocks, developers can ask for a wallet’s token balances, NFT holdings, transaction history, or prices and receive clean results across multiple chains, such as Ethereum, Polygon, Solana, and others. This cuts down the time to build wallets, portfolio trackers, NFT marketplaces, and analytics tools.

Other products support app development. Authentication lets users sign in with their wallets, Streams delivers real-time notifications about on-chain events, and node access and data APIs support decentralized finance and gaming projects. Documentation and SDKs help developers integrate quickly, and the platform handles indexing and scaling.

item.title: MOSTLY AI
item.description:
MOSTLY AI helps organizations use data that would otherwise be locked away by privacy rules. It trains a generative model on a real dataset, such as customer transactions or patient records, and then produces a new dataset that reflects the same patterns, relationships, and distributions but contains no real individuals. Banks, insurers, and healthcare companies use it to share data across teams and borders, test software, and develop models.

The platform handles multi-table relational data, preserving links between tables such as customers and their orders. Quality and privacy reports compare the synthetic data with the original and check for leakage, and features can rebalance datasets to reduce bias or fill in rare cases. An open-source SDK allows developers to run generation in their own environment, while the platform adds a user interface, scheduling, and enterprise controls.

item.title: MyFitnessPal
item.description:
MyFitnessPal is the best-known food diary app. You log what you eat by searching a database of packaged foods, restaurant meals, and homemade recipes, and the app totals calories and macronutrients against daily goals. It syncs with fitness trackers and apps, so exercise adjusts your targets, and it records weight and measurements over time. Millions of people use it for weight loss, muscle gain, or general awareness.

Its size is its strength. The food database is huge, though many entries are user-submitted and can contain errors, so it pays to choose verified items. Features include barcode scanning, recipe import, meal scanning with AI to log from a photo, and voice logging. Premium adds more detailed nutrient tracking, custom goals, macro presets, and meal planning, while a free version covers basic logging.

item.title: NAVEX
item.description:
NAVEX serves compliance and risk teams at large organizations. Its best-known service is a reporting hotline and web portal where employees can raise concerns about misconduct anonymously. Reports flow into a case management system that assigns investigators, tracks actions, and keeps records.

The company also provides policy management, training courses, third-party risk tools, and analytics that reveal patterns across reports. Newer features use AI to summarize cases, categorize reports, and surface trends for compliance leaders.

item.title: Nearmap
item.description:
Nearmap captures aerial photos from aircraft, covering large areas in populated regions, and refreshes them regularly. Users view and measure current imagery on a map, compare dates to see change over time, and download data for analysis.

AI turns pictures into data. Models detect features such as roof condition, solar panels, pools, vegetation, and building footprints, giving insurers, councils, and contractors information without visiting sites. The data is available through a web app, APIs, and integrations with GIS and other tools.

item.title: New Relic
item.description:
New Relic helps engineering teams understand how their software behaves in production. You add agents or OpenTelemetry instrumentation to your applications and infrastructure, and it collects performance data, errors, logs, and traces of requests as they move through services. Dashboards and alerts show slow endpoints, failing deployments, and resource pressure, and distributed tracing helps pinpoint which service in a chain caused a delay.

The platform covers application performance monitoring, infrastructure monitoring, log management, browser and mobile monitoring, and synthetic checks that test your site from outside. Applied intelligence groups related alerts and reduces noise, and an AI assistant lets people ask questions about their systems in plain language, summarize incidents, and get suggested next steps. It also includes tools for monitoring AI applications, tracking model calls, latency, cost, and quality.

item.title: Next Insurance
item.description:
NEXT Insurance focuses on small businesses such as contractors, consultants, cleaners, and shops. Instead of working with a broker, an owner answers a few questions online and gets a quote within minutes, buys the policy, and receives proof of insurance immediately. Digital certificates of insurance can be downloaded or sent to clients whenever needed, which saves time for tradespeople who must prove coverage to customers.

The company offers coverage lines such as general liability, professional liability, workers’ compensation, commercial auto, and tools and equipment. Its software uses data and automation to underwrite quickly and to handle policy changes and claims, with many tasks done in an app or on the website. The insurer is rated by industry agencies for financial strength.

item.title: Niantic Lightship
item.description:
Lightship began as a set of tools for building location-based AR experiences. The ARDK SDK for Unity offered features such as depth sensing, occlusion, and meshing, and the Visual Positioning System let apps determine a device’s precise location and orientation by matching camera images to a map of the real world. The technology came from the infrastructure behind Pokémon GO and drew on scans collected from players.

Niantic’s geospatial work later moved into a separate company, Niantic Spatial, after the games business was sold. The developer platform was renamed the Niantic Spatial Platform, with an SDK for Unity, tools for scanning places through Scaniverse, and mapping services. The original Lightship website was shut down, and visitors are redirected, with guidance for migrating projects.

item.title: Noom
item.description:
Noom approaches weight loss as a behavior change problem. After a quiz about your habits and goals, the app builds a plan and delivers short daily lessons based on cognitive behavioral therapy, covering topics like emotional eating, habits, and triggers. A food log uses a color system for food density instead of strict calorie bans, and the app tracks weight, steps, and water.

Support comes through coaching and community. Depending on the plan, users can message a coach, join groups, and use an AI assistant to ask questions and get guidance. Noom has expanded into medical weight management, offering clinician-supervised programs that may include prescription medication in some regions. Programs are meant to help people form sustainable habits.

item.title: Okta
item.description:
Okta is one of the best-known providers of cloud identity. Companies use it as the central place where employees sign in to their applications: one login gives access to hundreds of apps through single sign-on, and multi-factor authentication adds protection against stolen passwords. The Universal Directory stores identities and groups, and lifecycle management automates giving people the right access when they join, change roles, or leave.

The platform covers more of the identity problem over time. Adaptive policies check device and context before allowing access, governance tools handle access reviews and requests, and privileged access tools protect administrator accounts. Okta also owns Auth0 for customer-facing apps. As companies deploy AI agents that act on behalf of users, Okta has added features for giving these agents their own identities and managing what they may do.

item.title: OneTrust
item.description:
OneTrust helps large organizations manage the rules about data. Its best-known product handles consent: the cookie banners and preference centers that appear on websites and apps and record what visitors agree to. Privacy teams use other modules to respond to data subject requests such as access and deletion, map where personal data is stored, run privacy impact assessments, and show regulators that they follow laws like GDPR and CCPA.

The platform has expanded into broader governance, risk, and compliance. Tools cover third-party and vendor risk, security and IT risk, ethics and policy management, and environmental and social reporting. A growing area is AI governance: inventorying the AI systems an organization uses, assessing their risks, and tracking compliance with emerging rules such as the EU AI Act. AI features in the platform help classify data and automate assessments.

item.title: Osano
item.description:
Osano began with cookie consent, the banner that asks visitors what tracking they accept. Its consent manager scans a site, categorizes cookies and scripts, shows region-appropriate banners, and records choices, which helps companies comply with laws such as GDPR and CCPA. Websites install it with a small piece of code, and it can block scripts until a visitor agrees.

The platform grew to cover the wider privacy program. Tools handle data subject access requests, data mapping, and assessments, and a vendor monitoring service tracks the privacy practices of third parties and flags risks. Osano also offers privacy rating information and a catalog of vendor reports. Features for managing AI use and policies are being added as regulation develops.

item.title: Palmetto
item.description:
Palmetto connects homeowners with solar and energy services. A homeowner enters an address and gets an assessment of how much a system could save, compares financing options, and is matched with installers. The company also offers energy management that coordinates devices like batteries and EV chargers.

On the business side, Palmetto provides software and data used by installers, utilities, and fintechs, including tools for sizing systems, tracking incentives, and managing projects. AI helps optimize when to charge or use stored energy based on rates and weather.

item.title: Papercup
item.description:
Papercup offered dubbing for media companies. Its system translated the dialogue of a video and generated speech in another language that matched the tone and timing of the original, with human translators and editors checking the results. Publishers, broadcasters, and content owners used it to put news, documentaries, and entertainment in front of audiences in new markets without paying for traditional dubbing studios.

The approach mixed machine speed with human oversight. Linguists reviewed translations, adjusted phrasing, and corrected pronunciation, which kept quality higher than fully automatic dubbing and made the service suitable for professional content. It also let customers keep control over the voice style and brand.

item.title: Particle
item.description:
Particle gives hardware teams a full stack for connected devices. It sells development boards and production-ready modules with cellular, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth connectivity, runs its own device operating system, and provides a cloud console to monitor devices, send commands, and update firmware over the air. Because connectivity, SIM management, and cloud services come bundled, a small team can move from prototype to production without assembling the parts separately.

The platform emphasizes fleet management at scale. Dashboards show device health and data usage, alerts flag problems, and tools support provisioning, remote diagnostics, and secure updates. Webhooks and integrations send data to cloud services and applications, and newer products add more powerful edge computing, including boards that run Android and machine learning workloads at the edge.

item.title: PatSnap
item.description:
PatSnap serves teams that need to understand the patent landscape. Its search covers a very large collection of patents and scientific literature worldwide, and semantic search finds relevant documents from a description of an invention instead of exact keywords. Users can analyze who is filing in a technology area, map clusters of related patents, track competitors, and check whether an idea has been patented before.

Several products fit different jobs. Tools help with prior art searches before filing, freedom-to-operate checks before launching a product, and landscape analysis to guide R&D strategy. AI assistants summarize patents, extract key claims, and answer questions about a technology, and workflows let teams share results and collaborate. The platform also covers non-patent literature and market information for innovation scouting.

item.title: Persona
item.description:
Persona lets companies verify who their customers and business partners are. A business builds a flow, choosing which checks to run: collecting and verifying a government ID, matching a selfie to the photo with liveness detection, checking databases and watchlists, verifying a business and its owners, or confirming an address. The flow can adapt based on risk, asking for more evidence only when something looks suspicious.

Configurability sets it apart. Companies can design the user experience, set rules for approvals, and route uncertain cases to human reviewers in a case management tool. Additional products detect fraud patterns across accounts, run ongoing monitoring, and verify employees and workforce identities. APIs and no-code builders connect the flows to existing systems, and the platform covers documents from many countries.

item.title: Perspective API
item.description:
Perspective used machine learning to help moderate online conversations. A site sent a comment to the API and received scores for attributes such as toxicity, insult, profanity, and threat, which publishers and platforms used to flag comments for review, warn commenters before posting, or sort discussions. News organizations and forums used it to cope with large numbers of comments, and researchers used it to study online abuse.

The tool also sparked debate. Studies found that its scores could be biased, for example by rating comments mentioning certain identity terms as more toxic, and it was not a substitute for human moderators. Jigsaw acknowledged limitations and worked to reduce bias, and the model was widely used in research as a benchmark for toxicity.

item.title: Petcube
item.description:
Petcube sells connected cameras for people who want to check on pets while away. A camera with a wide-angle view streams video to a phone app, and two-way audio lets owners talk to the pet. Models differ in features: some include a built-in laser toy for play, some toss treats on command, and some are designed for indoor or outdoor use. Setup is through Wi-Fi and a smartphone.

Software adds intelligence. AI can detect when a pet is barking, moving, or when a person is in view, and send alerts, and a subscription provides cloud recording, event history, and access to veterinarians by video chat. Pet owners use it to keep an eye on anxious dogs, monitor cats, and share live views with family members.

item.title: PlanetScale
item.description:
PlanetScale brought a workflow familiar from Git to relational databases. Developers create a branch of their database schema, make changes, and merge them through a deploy request, with checks that avoid downtime. Behind that is Vitess, the sharding system created at YouTube, which lets MySQL scale horizontally across many servers. This allows growth beyond the limits of a single database machine.

Features focus on safe changes and performance. Online schema changes let teams alter large tables without locking, insights show slow queries and suggest improvements, and connection handling supports large numbers of clients. Recent products emphasize high-performance storage and have extended the platform to Postgres. AI-assisted insights help identify problematic queries, and the service integrates with popular frameworks and hosting platforms.

item.title: Postman
item.description: Postman started as a simple way to send HTTP requests without writing code, and it is still the most common tool for poking at an API. You enter a URL, choose a method, add headers and a body, and see the response. Requests are saved in collections that can be shared with a team, and environments let you switch variables like base URLs and keys between development, staging, and production without editing every request.

item.title: Procore
item.description:
Procore is one of the most widely used software platforms in construction. It gives everyone on a building project a shared place to manage drawings and documents, RFIs and submittals, daily logs, schedules, budgets, change orders, and inspections. Instead of email chains and spreadsheets, project information lives in one system with a record of who did what, which reduces disputes and rework.

The platform spans the project lifecycle, from preconstruction bidding and estimating through construction and closeout. Financial tools handle cost tracking, invoicing, and payments, while quality and safety modules support checklists, observations, and incident reports. A marketplace of integrations connects accounting, scheduling, and design tools. AI features help search across documents, summarize information, and automate routine tasks, and agents are being added to take on project management work.

item.title: PromptBase
item.description:
PromptBase turned prompts into products. Creators craft prompts that reliably produce a type of result, such as a particular art style, a logo format, or a structured business document, and list them with example outputs. Buyers pay a small amount to get the text, then use it with the relevant AI tool, saving time on trial and error.

The marketplace organizes prompts by model and category, shows sample images, and uses ratings and reviews to help buyers choose. It also supports custom prompt requests and tools for prompt creators to test and sell their work. The business sits on a belief that skilled prompting has value, particularly for image generators where small wording changes make a big difference.

item.title: PromptHero
item.description:
PromptHero started as a search engine for AI image prompts. You can browse a huge gallery of generated images, each shown with the prompt and settings that created it, and search for styles or subjects. That makes it a learning tool: you can see how others phrase things to get a certain look, and adapt their prompts to your own ideas.

The site has added features around the community. Users upload their creations, follow artists, and join challenges, and a generator lets you create images directly on the site using several models. Courses and guides teach prompt writing and workflow tips for different tools, and a paid tier offers more generations and features.

item.title: PrusaSlicer
item.description:
PrusaSlicer converts 3D models into the instructions a printer follows. You load a model, arrange it on the bed, choose a print profile for your printer and material, and the slicer generates the toolpaths, previewing each layer. It started as a fork of Slic3r and is developed by Prusa Research, which makes well-known 3D printers, and it is open source under the AGPL.

It’s valued for depth and control. Features include variable layer height, tree and organic supports, multi-material and multi-color printing, modifiers and custom settings for parts of a model, and a calibration toolkit. It supports printers from many manufacturers through profiles and a plugin-like configuration system, and has a mode that hides advanced settings for beginners. Community forks such as OrcaSlicer and Bambu Studio build on it.

item.title: RapidAPI
item.description:
RapidAPI made discovering APIs easier. Developers browse a catalog of thousands of APIs across categories such as weather, finance, sports, language, and AI, test them in the browser, and subscribe with a single key and billing account. This saves the effort of signing up with every provider separately, and API publishers get a distribution channel and billing.

The company also offered products for businesses, including an enterprise hub for managing internal and partner APIs, and testing tools. Nokia acquired the technology and marketplace to support its efforts to expose telecom network capabilities to developers through APIs, and the public marketplace is expected to continue much as before with some rebranding.

item.title: Readwise
item.description:
Readwise addresses a common frustration: highlighting passages and never seeing them again. It imports highlights from Kindle, Apple Books, Instapaper, Pocket-style services, podcasts, and PDFs into one library, and sends a daily review of a few of them by email or in the app, using spaced repetition so important ideas return at intervals.

The service integrates with the note-taking ecosystem, exporting highlights to Notion, Obsidian, Roam, Logseq, and others, so notes stay linked to sources. Search lets you find a highlight across everything you have read, and a mobile and browser extension make capture easy. Readwise also makes Reader, a read-it-later app, and AI features can summarize and let you chat with your highlights.

item.title: Ready Player Me
item.description: Ready Player Me offered a way to carry one avatar across many apps. A user took a selfie or built a character in the creator, customized clothing and hair, and received a 3D avatar that worked in a growing network of games, social platforms, and VR worlds. For developers, an SDK and web tools made it easy to add avatars without building a character creator from scratch, and it supported engines such as Unity and Unreal.

item.title: Recursion Pharmaceuticals
item.description: Recursion approaches drug discovery as a data problem. Its labs run enormous numbers of experiments in which cells are treated with genetic changes or compounds and photographed under microscopes. Machine learning analyzes the images to find how diseases change cell appearance and which compounds reverse those changes, building a large map of biology that the company calls the Recursion OS. The idea is to find promising targets and molecules faster than with traditional trial-and-error screening.

item.title: Repustate
item.description: Repustate focuses on understanding opinions in many languages. Its API reads text, such as tweets, reviews, news, or survey responses, and returns the sentiment, the topics and entities discussed, and the themes that recur, with attention to context so that sentiment about one aspect of a product can be separated from another. Language coverage is a selling point, including Arabic, Chinese, and many other languages that are less well served by some competitors.

item.title: Rookout
item.description:
Rookout solved a frustrating problem: figuring out what is happening inside production code. Normally, finding a bug means adding logging, redeploying, and waiting for the problem to recur. Rookout let developers set non-breaking breakpoints in live applications, so they could capture variable values, stack traces, and logs on demand without stopping the program or changing and restarting it.

It supported cloud-native environments with containers, serverless functions, and Kubernetes, and integrated with the tools developers already used for logging and monitoring. The data could be sent to existing observability systems, so debugging fit into current workflows. It was used by engineering teams that needed to debug complex, distributed applications quickly.

item.title: Root Insurance
item.description:
Root built its pitch on the idea that safe drivers should pay less. New customers take a test drive period with the app, which uses the phone’s sensors to measure things such as braking, speed, turning, and time of day driving. Combined with other information, those readings help set the price, so a careful driver can get a lower rate than under traditional pricing based mainly on demographics.

The process is online. People get a quote, buy a policy, and manage their coverage in the app, including proof of insurance and claims. Root also sells through partners, embedding insurance into other companies’ purchasing flows, and has added products such as renters insurance. Machine learning supports pricing, fraud detection, and claims handling.

item.title: Samsara
item.description:
Samsara collects data from the physical world and puts it to work. Gateways and cameras installed on vehicles, trailers, and equipment report location, engine data, driver behavior, and conditions, and the cloud platform presents it through dashboards and apps. Fleet managers use it for tracking, routing, maintenance, compliance with driver hours rules, and safety coaching.

AI dashcams detect risky events like distracted driving, tailgating, and rolling stops, and alert drivers and managers, and video evidence helps with accidents and insurance claims. The platform also covers equipment monitoring, site safety, temperature tracking for cold chains, and workflow tools such as digital forms and inspections. An AI assistant helps users analyze data and set up actions in plain language.

item.title: Satellogic
item.description:
Satellogic builds and operates its own satellites with the goal of making high-resolution imagery affordable and frequent. Its NewSat satellites capture sharp images and multispectral and hyperspectral data, and the company has emphasized low production costs, which allows it to launch many satellites and offer tasking and archive imagery. Customers use the data for mapping, agriculture, infrastructure monitoring, defense, and environmental analysis.

The company layers analytics on top of imagery. Machine learning detects objects and changes, such as new construction or vehicle movement, and produces insights at scale, and cloud tools and APIs let customers search the archive and request new captures. It also provides satellites and data to government customers for sovereign needs.

item.title: Schrödinger
item.description:
Schrödinger builds software that simulates molecules. Its approach relies on physics: calculating how atoms interact to predict properties like how strongly a drug candidate binds to a protein. The best-known method, free energy perturbation, estimates binding strength with accuracy useful enough to guide which molecules to make in the lab. Pharmaceutical and biotech companies use the platform to design and screen compounds before synthesizing them.

Machine learning is combined with these simulations. Models trained on simulation results can score vast numbers of molecules rapidly, which makes it possible to explore chemical space far beyond what physical calculations alone could cover. The software suite includes Maestro as the main interface and LiveDesign for collaboration among scientists, with applications in materials science, such as batteries and polymers, alongside life sciences.

item.title: Sentry
item.description:
Sentry tells developers when their code breaks and why. By adding an SDK to an app, errors are reported with stack traces, the environment, the user’s actions leading up to the problem, and the release that introduced it. Sentry groups duplicate errors into single issues, sends alerts, and links to the relevant commit, so teams can fix a bug quickly rather than discovering it from user complaints.

Beyond error tracking, Sentry monitors performance with tracing that shows slow requests and database queries, and session replay records what the user saw. Cron monitoring watches scheduled jobs, and release health tracks crash-free sessions. Its AI assistant, Seer, analyzes issues to suggest root causes and can propose fixes, and tools for monitoring AI applications trace model calls. It supports most languages and frameworks, and integrates with GitHub, Slack, and Jira.

item.title: Shorthand
item.description:
Shorthand makes it possible to create the kind of immersive web story that once required a design and development team. You assemble a story from sections with full-width images, video backgrounds, parallax effects, and text, and the platform handles responsive layout and animation. The finished piece is published as a webpage that scrolls like a magazine feature, and works on phones and desktops.

Newsrooms, universities, nonprofits, and corporate communications teams use it for long-form journalism, annual reports, campaign stories, and case studies. Collaboration features let writers and editors work together with review stages, brand themes keep designs consistent, and analytics show readership. Stories can be embedded in a site or hosted by Shorthand, and a CMS integration helps publishing.

item.title: Sight Machine
item.description:
Sight Machine tackles the data mess inside factories. Machines, sensors, and systems produce data in many formats, and plants often cannot easily combine it. Sight Machine’s platform pulls in data from equipment, quality systems, and enterprise software, standardizes it into a common model of the production process, and creates a digital twin that shows how products move through the plant.

With that foundation, teams can analyze performance. Dashboards track throughput, yield, scrap, and downtime across lines and sites, machine learning finds the factors that drive defects or slowdowns, and alerts flag issues in near real time. An AI assistant lets operators and engineers ask questions about production data in plain language, and the platform supports sustainability tracking such as energy use.

item.title: Spacemaker AI
item.description:
Spacemaker was a Norwegian startup that applied AI to the first phase of building design. Given a site and a set of goals, it generates many layouts for buildings, then analyzes each for sunlight, daylight, wind comfort, noise, views, and the amount of floor area it provides. Designers can compare options and adjust parameters, rather than testing a few ideas by hand.

Autodesk acquired the company and integrated its technology into Autodesk Forma, a cloud platform for early design. Forma combines site context, environmental analysis, and design tools, and connects to Revit and other Autodesk products so early decisions can be carried into detailed design. The platform serves architects, developers, and city planners evaluating projects.

item.title: Spire Global
item.description:
Spire builds and operates a large fleet of small satellites known as nanosatellites. Instead of taking photographs, they listen: they pick up radio signals from ships, aircraft, and GPS signals bouncing off the Earth, and measure atmospheric conditions. The resulting data feeds products that track vessels around the world, monitor air traffic, and improve weather forecasts.

The business sells data and analytics as a service. Maritime customers use it to follow ships, estimate arrival times, and detect suspicious behavior, aviation customers use it for flight tracking, and meteorological agencies use radio occultation data to enhance forecasts. Spire also provides space services, building and operating satellites for customers. Machine learning supports forecasting and anomaly detection in the data, and APIs deliver it to customers’ systems.

item.title: Spot.io
item.description:
Spot started as Spotinst, a company that helped users run workloads on cheap but interruptible cloud capacity. Its Elastigroup service predicts when spot instances will be reclaimed and moves workloads to keep applications running, which can reduce compute costs sharply. Ocean applies the same ideas to Kubernetes clusters, scaling nodes and choosing instance types automatically, and Eco manages savings plans and reserved instances.

NetApp acquired Spot, branded it Spot by NetApp, and later sold the Spot FinOps portfolio to Flexera, which now develops it alongside its other cloud cost tools. The tools support AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, with dashboards showing savings, and they are sold on a model tied to a percentage of savings or capacity. Customers have included engineering teams running large container and batch workloads.

item.title: Stats Perform
item.description:
Stats Perform collects detailed data about professional sports. Trained collectors and tracking technology record events in matches, such as passes, shots, and player positions, and the company supplies that information to broadcasters, media companies, sportsbooks, leagues, and clubs. Its Opta brand is widely seen in football statistics on television and websites. The data feeds power live scores, fantasy games, and graphics.

AI is used both to create data and to analyze it. Computer vision extracts player and ball tracking from video, which reduces the manual work of collecting information, and models predict outcomes, evaluate player performance, and estimate the value of actions on the field. Coaches and analysts use the tools for scouting and tactical analysis, while media and betting clients use predictions and content such as automated match summaries.

item.title: Stem AI
item.description:
Stem began by installing battery storage systems for businesses, and its software, Athena, became the heart of the company. Athena uses forecasts of energy prices, demand, and generation to decide when a battery should charge or discharge, balancing cost savings for the owner with revenue from grid services. This kind of optimization can make storage economically viable.

The business has shifted from selling hardware toward software and services. Athena manages solar plus storage, standalone batteries, and other distributed assets for developers and owners, and also offers analytics and asset performance tools. Machine learning helps predict conditions and handle the complexity of electricity markets, which differ by region.

item.title: Storybird
item.description:
Storybird approaches writing through pictures. Writers choose artwork from a library of illustrations and build a story around it, which lowers the barrier for young children who find a blank page daunting. The platform offers story types such as picture books, chapter books, and poetry, along with prompts and challenges to get ideas flowing, and finished stories can be published, shared, and read.

Education has been a major focus. Teachers use Storybird to run writing assignments, give feedback, and manage classes, with lessons, quizzes, and activities that support literacy skills. Students can write and publish in a safe, teacher-moderated environment. Newer features introduce AI assistance for prompts and feedback, with a focus on supporting rather than replacing the student’s writing.

item.title: StoryChief
item.description:
StoryChief helps marketing teams run a content workflow in one place. Teams plan content on a calendar, write articles in a shared editor, route them through review and approval, and then publish to multiple channels with a click, including their website, social networks, newsletters, and platforms like Medium. It reduces the work of copying content between tools and keeps assets organized.

SEO and analytics features support performance. An optimizer scores drafts against target keywords, and reports track traffic and engagement across channels. AI features help generate outlines and drafts, rewrite content, and adapt posts for social networks, and a library of integrations connects WordPress, HubSpot, and other tools. It’s popular with agencies that manage multiple clients, and with in-house teams.

item.title: TaxJar
item.description:
TaxJar tackles the complexity of U.S. sales tax for online businesses. Rules differ by state, county, and city, and a seller can owe tax in many places once they pass certain thresholds. TaxJar connects to selling channels such as Shopify, Amazon, WooCommerce, and BigCommerce, pulls in sales data, calculates the tax owed, and shows where the business has obligations. Reports summarize what is due in each jurisdiction.

The service can also file and remit returns in many states for an additional fee, which saves sellers from dealing with each state’s portal. An API provides tax calculations at checkout for platforms and developers. It was acquired by Stripe, which has been building its own tax product, Stripe Tax, and TaxJar continues to operate and support filing, while its role is evolving alongside Stripe’s tools.

item.title: Teladoc Health
item.description:
Teladoc Health delivers healthcare through phones and video. Members can see a clinician for common conditions, get prescriptions where appropriate, and access specialists, therapists, and dermatologists without traveling. Employers and health plans buy the service for their members, which makes access fast and convenient for non-emergency issues, and it includes expert medical opinion services and virtual nursing.

The company also runs programs for chronic conditions, such as diabetes and hypertension, combining connected devices, coaching, and digital tools. Mental health care is a major area, including its consumer therapy brand BetterHelp. AI is used for matching patients with providers, supporting clinicians with documentation, and personalizing care programs.

item.title: TestFit
item.description:
TestFit speeds up the feasibility stage of real estate development. A user draws a site boundary and sets rules such as unit mix, parking ratios, setbacks, and building types, and TestFit generates layouts that fit, updating in real time as constraints change. It reports metrics like unit counts, parking, rentable area, and efficiency, which let developers judge whether a site works before investing heavily.

It handles multiple product types, including apartment buildings, townhomes, self-storage, hotels, and parking structures, and exports to common design tools such as Revit and CAD for the next stage. Cost and revenue features help assess returns, and collaboration tools let teams share scenarios. Generative algorithms explore many arrangements to find efficient solutions.

item.title: Testim
item.description:
Testim addresses one of the biggest pain points in test automation: tests that break whenever the interface changes. Instead of relying on a single brittle identifier for each element, it uses machine learning to learn multiple attributes of each element, so the test can still find a button after a developer renames or moves it. This self-healing behavior reduces the time engineers spend fixing tests.

Tests can be recorded by clicking through an app, then edited visually or with code for custom logic. The platform runs tests in the cloud across browsers and integrates with CI/CD tools, issue trackers, and test management systems, so test results fit into existing workflows. Features such as grouping and reusable steps help teams scale suites, and AI assists with test creation and failure analysis.

item.title: Tinybeans
item.description:
Tinybeans is a place to keep a child’s growing-up record. Parents upload photos, videos, and short notes, and they appear in a private timeline organized by date and by child. Selected family members, such as grandparents, are invited to view and comment, which keeps updates off public social networks while sharing moments with those who care.

Features help preserve memories. Milestone tracking prompts parents to note first steps and other events, a calendar shows memories on this day, and storage keeps content safe over the years. A premium plan adds unlimited uploads and the ability to order photo books, calendars, and prints. AI helps organize and suggest highlights.

item.title: Tonic AI
item.description:
Tonic.ai solves a common development problem: engineers need realistic data to test software, but production data contains sensitive information. Tonic Structural connects to a database, identifies sensitive fields, and replaces them with fake but realistic values, preserving relationships and formats so applications behave as they would with real data. This allows teams to build and test with representative data without exposing customers’ details.

Other products broaden the range. Tonic Fabricate generates synthetic data from scratch for new applications or demos, and Tonic Textual finds and redacts sensitive information in unstructured data such as documents and text, which helps prepare data for training or retrieval in AI systems. Integrations support popular databases and data warehouses, and subsetting tools cut large databases down to smaller, usable test sets.

item.title: Transcend
item.description:
Transcend takes a developer-oriented approach to privacy compliance. It connects to a company’s databases, SaaS tools, and warehouses to discover where personal data is stored, then automates responses to requests from individuals to access or delete their data. Instead of manually searching dozens of systems, the platform executes the request across them and keeps a record.

Other products cover related needs. Consent management controls cookies and tracking according to each visitor’s choices and location, a gateway can enforce those choices in what data flows to third parties, and data mapping documents processing activities. Newer tools address AI governance, helping teams track what data feeds models and meet emerging regulations.

item.title: Tripadvisor
item.description:
Tripadvisor built its name on traveler reviews. Visitors rate and describe hotels, restaurants, tours, and sights, and the site ranks places based on those opinions, which people use to decide where to stay and eat. Photos, forums, and Q&A add detail. It covers millions of places worldwide and is free to browse.

The site has developed into a booking and planning platform. It compares hotel prices and links to booking partners, sells tours and activities through Viator, and supports restaurant reservations through TheFork. AI trip-planning features create itineraries from a short description, suggest places based on reviews, and organize saved items into trips. Businesses use Tripadvisor to manage their listings, respond to reviews, and advertise.

item.title: Tulip
item.description:
Tulip brings software to the factory floor. Engineers and operators build apps using a drag-and-drop editor, with steps that guide workers through assembly, inspection, or maintenance, collect data, and trigger actions. Connecting sensors, machines, and tools lets the apps read real-time values, and the platform replaces clipboards and spreadsheets with digital work instructions and quality checks.

Analytics and automation extend the value. Dashboards show production performance, quality, and downtime, and machine learning models can detect anomalies or predict issues. Generative AI helps create apps from a description and analyze data in plain language. As a lightweight manufacturing execution system, it can be adopted gradually, line by line.

item.title: Turbonomic
item.description: Turbonomic tries to answer a question that infrastructure teams face constantly: is each application getting the resources it needs without wasting money? The platform monitors applications and the infrastructure they run on, including virtual machines, containers, and cloud services, and uses analytics to decide where workloads should run, how large they should be, and when to scale. It can take actions automatically, such as resizing instances, moving workloads, or adjusting Kubernetes resources.

item.title: TurboTax
item.description: TurboTax makes tax filing a guided interview. You answer plain-language questions, import documents like W-2s and 1099s, and the software fills in the forms, checks for errors, and estimates your refund or amount owed. It supports many situations, from simple returns to investments, self-employment, and rental income, and e-files returns with federal and state tax agencies. It has long been the most recognized brand in consumer tax software in the U.S.

item.title: Uplight
item.description:
Uplight helps utilities communicate with customers and manage demand. It combines data on how households and businesses use energy with tools for personalized messages, home energy reports, smart thermostat programs, and marketplace offers for efficient appliances. The goal is to reduce peak demand and help customers cut bills, which lowers the need for expensive new capacity.

By acquiring AutoGrid, Uplight added software for managing distributed energy resources such as batteries, solar, EV chargers, and flexible loads. Together, the platform can enroll customers, control devices, and optimize their use as a virtual power plant, supported by machine learning for forecasting and targeting. It serves electric and gas utilities in many regions.

item.title: Virtuous
item.description:
Virtuous aims to help nonprofits treat donors as individuals. Its CRM unifies donor records, giving history, communications, and activity from the website and email, and uses scoring to show which supporters are likely to give again or give more. Fundraisers use the data to plan outreach and prioritize relationships, rather than sending the same message to everyone.

Additional tools expand the system. Marketing automation builds journeys and email campaigns triggered by donor behavior, online giving forms and text-to-give accept gifts, and volunteer management tracks service. Newer AI features help write appeals, summarize donor histories, and recommend next steps for each supporter, and an analytics layer shows campaign performance.

item.title: Wanderlog
item.description:
Wanderlog combines a travel notebook with a map. You create a trip, add places such as hotels, restaurants, and attractions, and arrange them by day. The app shows everything on a map with travel times between stops, and can optimize the order to reduce backtracking. It imports reservations from your email, tracks expenses, and works offline on mobile apps, which is handy while traveling.

Collaboration is a main feature. Friends and family can edit the same itinerary at once, vote on places, and share notes and budgets. AI tools suggest destinations and activities, generate draft itineraries from a few preferences, and recommend nearby places based on reviews and guides. A catalog of lists and guides provides inspiration for popular destinations.

item.title: Weglot
item.description:
Weglot lets a site add languages without rebuilding it. You install a plugin or add a snippet, Weglot finds the text on your pages, translates it with machine translation, and creates versions of the site in the languages you choose. It also adds a language switcher and handles the technical parts of international SEO such as hreflang tags and translated URLs.

Quality control happens in a dashboard. You can edit any translation, use a glossary to keep brand terms the same, and order professional translations through partners for key pages. Translations are stored and reused, and visual editing lets you fix text in the context of the page. AI features improve consistency, and it works with many popular platforms.

item.title: Whistle
item.description:
Whistle sold small GPS devices that attached to a pet’s collar and reported location through cellular networks. Owners could set safe zones, get an alert when a pet left them, and view recent routes. The devices also tracked activity, rest, and behaviors such as scratching and licking, and the app compared these against typical patterns to point out possible health changes.

The company was owned by Mars Petcare before Tractive, an Austrian pet tracking company, took over the brand. Rather than run two competing platforms, Tractive shut down the Whistle service, and the trackers no longer work. Tractive offered affected customers a replacement device, so owners are generally pointed to its products.

item.title: Whoop
item.description: WHOOP is a screenless wearable worn on the wrist or in apparel. It records heart rate, heart rate variability, skin temperature, blood oxygen, and movement around the clock, and its app turns that into daily scores for recovery, strain, and sleep. The idea is to show how prepared your body is to train hard or rest, and to give athletes and health-conscious people a sense of how habits like alcohol or late nights affect them.

item.title: Wingman
item.description:
Wingman positions itself as a coach for dating apps. A user shares their profile or chat, and the AI suggests better photos, rewrites the bio, and proposes replies to messages. The aim is to help people present themselves well and keep conversations going.

AI-written messages raise authenticity questions, since the person on the other end expects to talk to you. Many users prefer feedback and ideas to full ghostwriting. Sharing screenshots of chats involves other people’s messages, so consider privacy.

item.title: Wiz
item.description: Wiz became one of the fastest-growing security companies by making cloud risk easier to see. It connects to cloud accounts through APIs and snapshots, without installing agents on every machine, and builds a graph of resources, identities, networks, and data. From that graph it finds problems such as exposed storage, over-permissive roles, unpatched software, and secrets in code, and it shows how they could be chained together into an attack path to something valuable.

item.title: Woebot
item.description:
Woebot was one of the best-known mental health chatbots. It talked with users about mood and thoughts, using techniques from cognitive behavioral therapy to help them notice patterns, challenge unhelpful beliefs, and practice coping skills. Conversations were short and structured, with a friendly tone, so people could use it when they felt stressed or anxious, at any time of day.

It differed from general chatbots by using carefully written, clinically reviewed content instead of free-form generation, and the company ran studies to evaluate it. It aimed to make support more accessible and affordable than traditional therapy, and was used by individuals, employers, and health systems. It was always described as a supplement to, not a replacement for, professional care.

item.title: Wysa
item.description: Wysa is a conversational app for stress, low mood, and anxiety. Users chat with a friendly penguin character that asks about how they feel and offers exercises, such as reframing negative thoughts, breathing techniques, sleep tools, and guided meditations. The responses draw on structured therapeutic content written and reviewed by clinicians instead of unconstrained text generation, which is meant to make it safer and more predictable than a general chatbot.

item.title: XMind
item.description:
XMind is a long-standing mind mapping tool known for its range of layouts. Start with a central idea and branch outward, or switch to another structure such as a logic chart, fishbone diagram, matrix, tree chart, or timeline to fit the problem. It has a polished interface, attractive themes, and features such as markers, stickers, notes, and attachments, and it works offline.

Special modes help with presentation and organization. Brainstorming mode captures ideas quickly, outline view turns a map into a list, and Zen mode removes distractions. A presentation feature plays the map as a slideshow, and exports cover PDF, images, Word, and Markdown. AI features can generate a map from a topic, expand a branch with suggestions, and summarize content into a structure.

item.title: Zebra Medical Vision
item.description:
Zebra Medical Vision developed AI that reads medical scans and flags findings. Its algorithms examined chest X-rays, CT scans, and mammograms for conditions such as lung nodules, bone density loss, fatty liver, coronary calcium, and signs of fractures, often picking up incidental findings that a radiologist focused on another question might not report. The company had several algorithms cleared by regulators in the United States and Europe.

A distinctive aspect was population health analysis: by screening scans that were already taken for other purposes, hospitals could identify patients at risk of conditions such as osteoporosis or cardiovascular disease and follow up. Zebra Medical Vision offered its tools through a cloud platform that integrated with radiology workflows.

item.title: Feedzai
item.description:
Feedzai provides real-time fraud detection for banks, card issuers, and payment companies. Its models look at each transaction along with customer and device behavior and decide in milliseconds whether to approve, block, or send it for review. Flagging account takeover, card fraud, and scams quickly limits losses.

The platform also covers anti-money laundering and customer risk, combining signals from different parts of a bank in a single view. Case management tools help investigators work alerts, and explainability features show why a decision was made, which matters to regulators. Newer work addresses authorized scams where customers are tricked into sending money.

item.title: Forta
item.description:
Forta provides security monitoring for blockchain applications. Independent developers write detection bots that scan transactions and state changes across networks, looking for patterns that signal attacks, such as sudden fund movements or unusual contract calls. Bots publish alerts to the network, which protocols and users can subscribe to.

Machine learning models are used for some detections, such as spotting scams or anomalies. Protocols use Forta alerts to trigger their own responses, such as pausing contracts. A marketplace of bots covers many threat types and chains, and its token supports staking and rewards for bot operators.

item.title: iNaturalist
item.description:
iNaturalist is a citizen science project and app. Users upload photos or sounds of organisms they find, a computer vision model suggests what species it is, and other observers weigh in. When enough people agree, the observation reaches research grade, and the data is shared with scientific databases.

The result is one of the largest collections of biodiversity observations. Researchers use it to track species ranges, detect invasive species, and study changes over time. Projects and bioblitz events organize community efforts, and schools use it for nature education.

item.title: Kasisto
item.description:
Kasisto builds AI assistants for banks. Its KAI technology understands banking questions and can carry out actions, such as showing recent transactions, transferring funds, or explaining a fee, in a chat within a bank’s mobile app or website. The language models are tuned to the vocabulary and rules of finance.

A newer product, KAI Answers, uses generative AI to answer questions from a bank’s own policies and documents, with citations so staff and customers can see the source. Banks use it to cut call volumes and improve self-service, and the company has worked with institutions around the world.

item.title: Personetics
item.description:
Personetics supplies the intelligence behind money management features in banking apps. Banks connect transaction data, and the platform generates timely, personalized messages and suggestions, like warning a customer that a bill will overdraw their account or noticing a good time to save.

The aim is a more engaging and useful banking relationship. Personetics works with large banks around the world and presents itself as a way to turn data into proactive guidance. AI generates the insights and chooses when and how to show them.

item.title: Zest AI
item.description:
Zest AI helps lenders approve more borrowers safely. Its models use many variables to estimate credit risk, aiming to include people thin credit files would exclude while keeping losses in check. Lenders deploy the models in their own decisioning workflows.

Explainability is central, since regulators require lenders to give reasons for adverse decisions. Zest provides tools to explain scores and to test models for disparate impact across groups. Credit unions and community banks are among its customers.

item.title: Brex
item.description:
Brex built a corporate card and spend platform for startups and growing companies. Businesses issue cards to employees with set limits, and expenses are captured and matched automatically, with receipts collected through the app and policies enforced in real time. Finance teams get visibility into spending and can close their books faster than with manual expense reports.

The platform grew into a broader finance system. It includes bill payments, reimbursements, travel booking, banking features, and budgeting, with integrations to accounting software such as NetSuite and QuickBooks. AI agents handle tasks such as filling out expense reports, checking receipts for policy violations, and answering finance questions, aiming to reduce time spent on back-office work.

item.title: ContractPodAi
item.description:
ContractPodAi was built for corporate legal departments that handle large volumes of contracts. Its platform covers the lifecycle: drafting from templates, routing for approval, negotiation, signature, storage in a searchable repository, and tracking of obligations and renewals. It connects with systems such as Salesforce, Microsoft 365, and ERP tools so contracts sit within the business processes they relate to.

The company has rebranded as Leah, after the name of its AI product, and now describes itself as an agentic AI platform. Its AI agents review contracts against playbooks, flag risks and deviations, extract key terms, answer questions about a contract portfolio, and handle repetitive tasks across legal, procurement, and finance. The change reflects a wider move in legal technology from software that stores documents to software that does the first pass of the work.

item.title: ContractSafe
item.description:
ContractSafe addresses a basic business problem: contracts scattered across inboxes, shared drives, and filing cabinets. Teams upload agreements into one searchable repository, and the system reads them to pull out key details such as parties, effective dates, renewal terms, and notice periods. Because the text is searchable, finding a specific clause across hundreds of contracts takes seconds instead of hours.

Automation helps avoid missed deadlines. ContractSafe can send alerts before a contract renews or expires, so teams can renegotiate or cancel in time instead of being locked into automatic renewals. Permissions control who can see sensitive agreements, and reports summarize the portfolio by type, value, and upcoming dates. Integrations connect with tools such as Salesforce and Microsoft or Google storage, and an audit trail records activity.

item.title: Darktrace
item.description: Darktrace takes a different approach from signature-based security. Instead of matching known threats, it learns the usual patterns of each organization, such as which devices talk to which systems and how people normally log in, and then notices when something deviates. This lets it detect novel attacks and insider threats that do not match a known signature. The learning happens inside the customer’s environment, and Darktrace says it does not need to share data with a central model to do it.

item.title: Lever
item.description:
Lever pairs two things that recruiting teams often keep separate: an applicant tracking system for people who apply, and a relationship manager for people you want to attract. In one place, recruiters post jobs, move candidates through stages, schedule interviews, collect feedback, and build talent pools for roles that open later. The pipeline view is visual and quick to scan, which suits teams that hire continuously.

Sourcing and nurture are a focus. Lever can run email sequences to passive candidates, track responses, and bring prospects into the same pipeline as applicants. Interview scheduling is automated so recruiters spend less time on calendars, and scorecards keep feedback structured. Reporting covers the funnel, diversity data, and time to hire. Integrations link it to job boards, HR systems, and assessment tools.

item.title: Mercury
item.description: Mercury provides online banking designed for startups. A founder can open a business account in minutes, get checking and savings, send and receive wires and ACH transfers, issue virtual and physical debit and credit cards, and pay bills, all in a clean web and mobile interface. Mercury is a financial technology company, not a bank itself, and works with partner banks to hold deposits and provide FDIC insurance through sweep arrangements.

item.title: SmartRecruiters
item.description:
SmartRecruiters is an applicant tracking system built for large companies. Recruiters post jobs to many boards, receive and manage applications, collaborate with hiring managers on evaluations, schedule interviews, and extend offers, all in one workflow. A marketplace of integrations connects background checks, assessments, video interviewing, and HR systems, which suits global companies with complex hiring needs.

AI features support sourcing and screening. The platform recommends candidates from existing applicants and external pools, scores fit against job requirements, and helps with scheduling and communication. Its AI assistant can draft job descriptions and summarize candidate profiles, and analytics show the hiring funnel, time to fill, and diversity metrics. The company states it emphasizes transparency in how AI recommendations are made.

item.title: Viz.ai
item.description:
Viz.ai is known for its stroke software. When a patient has a CT scan that may show a large vessel occlusion, a blockage in a major brain artery, the AI analyzes the images within minutes and alerts the stroke team on their phones, with images they can view immediately. Speeding up that notification can cut the time to treatment, which matters in stroke, where each minute affects outcomes.

The platform has expanded beyond stroke. It supports other conditions, including pulmonary embolism, aortic disease, and heart conditions, and uses AI to identify patients who may be eligible for treatment or follow-up. A care coordination layer links hospitals, so specialists at a distance can review cases, communicate, and arrange transfers. Several of its algorithms have received regulatory clearance in the United States.

item.title: Voiceflow
item.description:
Voiceflow lets teams design conversational agents together. On a visual canvas, designers and developers map out how an agent should respond, add steps that call language models, search knowledge bases, run logic, and connect to APIs and tools. Non-engineers can shape conversations while developers handle integrations, which makes it practical for cross-functional teams in customer support, sales, and operations.

The platform handles the whole lifecycle. You can add a knowledge base of company content so the agent answers from it, test the agent in a built-in environment, and deploy it to a website, messaging channels, phone lines, or via API. Analytics and transcripts show how conversations go, and versioning and collaboration features support teamwork. Voiceflow works with a choice of language models.

item.title: Workable
item.description:
Workable is an applicant tracking system aimed at small and mid-sized companies. Recruiters create a job, post it to many job boards with one click, and manage candidates through a pipeline with scorecards, notes, and team collaboration. A careers page and templates for emails, offers, and interview kits cover the basics of hiring.

AI features speed up repetitive work. The platform can write job descriptions, suggest candidates from a large database and from your own applicants, screen resumes against criteria, and summarize interview recordings and notes. An AI assistant helps recruiters draft messages and prepare interview questions. Integrations connect to HR systems, calendars, background check providers, and assessment tools.

item.title: AI Aware
item.description:
AI Aware presents itself as a tool for checking whether content was written or generated by AI. Users upload a document or paste text, and the service returns an estimate of how likely it is to be machine-generated, along with detail on which parts raised the score. The idea is to give educators, publishers, and businesses a quick way to screen material.

Detection of AI-generated content is a difficult problem. Detectors rely on statistical patterns that can also appear in human writing, especially in formal or non-native text, and they can be fooled by editing or paraphrasing. For that reason, any score should be treated as a hint that calls for further review rather than as proof.

item.title: FastBots
item.description:
FastBots lets small businesses add a chatbot without developers. A user points the platform at their website, uploads files, or adds frequently asked questions, and it builds a bot that answers customers using that content. The bot is embedded with a snippet of code or connected to channels such as messaging apps.

Additional features include lead capture, handoff to a human, conversation history, and analytics on what visitors ask. Customization options control the look, tone, and behavior of the bot, and integrations send data to other tools. It is positioned as a quick setup for support and sales questions.

item.title: Ghostwall
item.description:
Ghostwall belongs to the group of click fraud prevention tools. Advertisers who pay per click can lose money when bots or competitors click ads. The service watches traffic to paid campaigns, looks for suspicious patterns, and blocks the sources that appear fraudulent, for example by adding them to exclusion lists on ad platforms.

Reports show blocked clicks and estimated savings. The ad platforms filter some invalid traffic themselves, so independent tools add value mainly for accounts with significant spend or visible fraud problems. Results depend on how good the detection is, and aggressive blocking can also exclude real customers.

item.title: Ideamap
item.description:
Ideamap lets users start with a topic and watch a map grow. The AI suggests branches, groups related ideas, and links concepts, so brainstorming moves beyond a first list. Users can edit nodes by hand, add notes, and rearrange the canvas.

Typical uses include planning projects, outlining articles, studying a subject, and mapping product ideas. The tool aims to reduce the friction of starting from a blank canvas and help with the organizing step that follows brainstorming.

item.title: MOVA Guide
item.description:
MOVA Guide gives recommendations through conversation. Instead of scrolling through lists of top-rated places, a user tells it something like I want a quiet evening with good food, and it suggests spots matching that mood in their area. It aims to feel more personal than review sites.

The app is aimed at both tourists and residents bored with their usual routine. Suggestions can include restaurants, cafes, activities, and events, and the guide adjusts as the user reacts to ideas.

item.title: PrompTessor
item.description:
PrompTessor gives prompt writers a place to work. Users draft a prompt, get suggestions to improve its structure and clarity, run it against several models, and compare outputs. Analysis tools point out ambiguity and missing context.

Typical users are people who build assistants and automations and need consistent behavior, as well as individuals who want better results from chatbots. Saving and versioning prompts helps teams reuse what works.

Independent information is limited. As models get better at understanding short requests, built-in prompt improvers in chat apps cover some needs. PrompTessor has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include PromptPerfect, PromptLayer, Promptfoo, LangSmith playground, and Anthropic’s prompt tools. PrompTessor suits users who iterate on prompts.

item.title: scalerX
item.description:
ScalerX targets communities and small businesses on Telegram. A user connects a knowledge source, such as documents or a website, configures an agent’s personality and rules, and launches a bot in Telegram that answers questions from that content.

Use cases include customer support, community moderation and FAQs, and onboarding for projects, especially in crypto and creator groups where Telegram is central. No-code setup lowers the barrier.

Independent information is limited, and bots must be tested to avoid wrong answers in public groups. ScalerX has a free tier and paid plans. Alternatives include Botpress, Chatbase, ManyChat, Voiceflow, and Telegram bot frameworks. ScalerX suits community managers deploying Telegram bots.
